title.raw: 卷一 本紀第一: 高祖上 Volume 1: Emperor Wu 1

sentences.zh: 陳書卷一

translations.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 1
translations.idiomatic: Book of Chen, Volume 1

sentences.zh: 本紀第一

translations.literal: Basic Annals, Number One
translations.idiomatic: Annals, Part One

sentences.zh: 高祖上

translations.literal: The Founder (Part One)
translations.idiomatic: The Founder, Part One

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝諱霸先，字興國，小字法生，吳興長城下若里人，漢太丘長陳寔之後也。

translations.literal: The Founder, Emperor Wu, had the tabooed name Baxian, the style name Xingguo, and the childhood name Fasheng. He was a native of Xiaruo Lane, Changcheng, Wuxing, and a descendant of Chen Shi, Magistrate of Taqiu in Han.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder, Emperor Wu, whose personal name was tabooed as Baxian, styled himself Xingguo and was known in youth as Fasheng. He came from Xiaruo Lane in Changcheng, Wuxing, and traced his line to Chen Shi, magistrate of Taqiu in Han times.

sentences.zh: 世居潁川。

translations.literal: For generations the clan dwelt in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family had lived in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 寔玄孫準，晉太尉。

translations.literal: Shi's great-great-grandson Zhun was Grand Commandant of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shi's great-great-grandson Zhun rose to be Grand Commandant of Jin.

sentences.zh: 準生匡，匡生達，永嘉南遷，為丞相掾，歷太子洗馬，出為長城令，悅其山水，遂家焉。

translations.literal: Zhun begat Kuang; Kuang begat Da. In the Yongjia era they migrated south. Da became an aide to the Chancellor, served successively as Palace Attendant to the Heir Apparent, went out as Magistrate of Changcheng, delighted in its mountains and waters, and settled his household there.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun's son was Kuang, and Kuang's son was Da. When the Yongjia turmoil drove the clan south, Da served as a chancellor's aide and then as attendant to the crown prince before being posted as magistrate of Changcheng. Charmed by the landscape, he made his home there.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂所親曰：「此地山川秀麗，當有王者興，二百年後，我子孫必鍾斯運。

translations.literal: He once told those close to him: "The mountains and rivers of this place are splendid; a king will surely rise here. Two hundred years hence, my descendants will surely be granted this destiny.
translations.idiomatic: He once told his intimates, "These mountains and streams are magnificent—a king will rise here. Two hundred years from now, my descendants will share in that fortune.

sentences.zh: 」達生康，復為丞相掾，咸和中土斷，故為長城人。

translations.literal: " Da begat Kang, who again served as an aide to the Chancellor. In the Xianhe era the native register was discontinued, and henceforth they were accounted people of Changcheng.
translations.idiomatic: " Da's son was Kang, who again served as a chancellor's aide. After the household register was broken off in the Xianhe era, the line was reckoned as Changcheng people.

sentences.zh: 康生盱眙太守英，英生尚書郎公弼，公弼生步兵校尉鼎，鼎生散騎侍郎高，高生懷安令詠，詠生安成太守猛，猛生太常卿道巨，道巨生皇考文讚。

translations.literal: Kang begat Ying, Administrator of Xuyi; Ying begat Gongbi, Gentleman Attendant at the Masters of Writing; Gongbi begat Ding, Colonel of Foot Soldiers; Ding begat Gao, Attendant Gentleman-Companion in Ordinary; Gao begat Yong, Magistrate of Huai'an; Yong begat Meng, Administrator of Ancheng; Meng begat Daoju, Chamberlain for Ceremonials; Daoju begat the Founder's father Wenzan.
translations.idiomatic: Kang's son Ying became administrator of Xuyi. Ying's son Gongbi served as a gentleman attendant in the Masters of Writing. Gongbi's son Ding was colonel of foot soldiers. Ding's son Gao was an attendant gentleman-companion in ordinary. Gao's son Yong was magistrate of Huai'an. Yong's son Meng was administrator of Ancheng. Meng's son Daoju was chamberlain for ceremonials. Daoju's son was the Founder's father, Wenzan.

sentences.zh: 高祖以梁天監二年癸未歲生。

translations.literal: The Founder was born in the guiwei year, the second year of Tianjian of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder was born in 503 CE, the guiwei year of Emperor Wu of Liang's Tianjian reign.

sentences.zh: 少俶儻有大志，不治生產。

translations.literal: In youth he was unconstrained and ambitious, and did not manage the household estate.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was free-spirited and ambitious, with no taste for managing the family livelihood.

sentences.zh: 既長，讀兵書，多武藝，明達果斷，為當時所推服。

translations.literal: Once grown, he read books of war, mastered many martial arts, was clear-sighted and decisive, and was admired by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he studied military writings and became skilled in many arms. Clear-minded, resolute, and decisive, he won the respect of all around him.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺五寸，日角龍顏，垂手過膝。

translations.literal: His height was seven feet five inches; he had a sun-horn and dragon countenance, and his hands hung past his knees.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven feet five inches tall, with the sun-horn and dragon-countenance of imperial portent; when he stood at ease, his hands reached below his knees.

sentences.zh: 嘗遊義興，館於許氏，夜夢天開數丈，有四人朱衣捧日而至，令高祖開口納焉，及覺，腹中猶熱，高祖心獨負之。

translations.literal: Once, traveling in Yixing, he lodged with the Xu family. That night he dreamed the sky opened several zhang, and four men in vermilion robes came bearing the sun, bidding the Founder open his mouth to receive it. When he awoke, his belly was still warm; the Founder alone kept this to himself.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while traveling in Yixing, he stayed with the Xu household. In the night he dreamed that the heavens split open for several yards and four men in crimson robes bore the sun to him, commanding him to open his mouth and take it in. When he woke, his belly was still warm. The Founder told no one and bore the omen in silence.

sentences.zh: 大同初，新喻侯蕭谟為吳興太守，[1]甚重高祖，嘗目高祖謂僚佐曰：「此人方將遠大。

translations.literal: In the early Datong era, Marquis of Xinyu Xiao Mo was Administrator of Wuxing.[1] He thought highly of the Founder and once fixed his gaze on him, telling his staff: "This man will go far.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Datong era, Xiao Mo, Marquis of Xinyu, served as administrator of Wuxing.[1] He held the Founder in high regard and once studied him closely before telling his aides, "This man is destined for great things.

sentences.zh: 」及谟為廣州刺史，高祖為中直兵參軍，隨府之鎮。

translations.literal: " When Mo became Inspector of Guangzhou, the Founder served as Middle Straight Troops Staff Officer and accompanied the headquarters to its post.
translations.idiomatic: " When Mo was appointed inspector of Guangzhou, the Founder became a staff officer in the middle straight troops and went with the headquarters to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 谟令高祖招集士馬，红至千人，仍命高祖監宋隆郡。

translations.literal: Mo ordered the Founder to gather gentlemen and horses until his force reached a thousand men, and then appointed him to oversee Songlong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Mo had the Founder recruit men and horses until he had assembled a force of a thousand, then put him in charge of Songlong commandery.

sentences.zh: 所部安化二縣元不賓，高祖討平之。

translations.literal: Within his jurisdiction the two counties of Anhua would not submit; the Founder attacked and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: The two counties of Anhua within his jurisdiction refused to submit; the Founder campaigned against them and brought them to order.

sentences.zh: 尋監西江督護、高要郡守。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was made Supervisor of the West River Defense Command and Administrator of Gaoyao.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed supervisor of the West River defense command and administrator of Gaoyao.

sentences.zh: 先是，武林侯蕭諮為交州刺史，以裒刻失红心，土人李賁連結數州豪傑同時反，臺遣高州刺史孫冏、新州刺史盧子雄將兵擊之，冏等不時進，皆於廣州伏誅。

translations.literal: Earlier, Marquis of Wulin Xiao Zi had been Inspector of Jiaozhou. Through harsh exactions he lost the hearts of the people. The native leader Li Ben joined with magnates of several commanderies and rose in rebellion at the same time. The court sent Sun Tong, Inspector of Gaozhou, and Lu Zixiong, Inspector of Xinzhou, with troops to attack him. Tong and the others did not advance in time and were all executed at Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xiao Zi, Marquis of Wulin, had served as inspector of Jiaozhou. His grinding exactions cost him the people's loyalty. The local leader Li Ben rallied powerful men across several provinces in simultaneous revolt. The court dispatched Sun Tong of Gaozhou and Lu Zixiong of Xinzhou with armies against him, but they failed to advance promptly and were all put to death at Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子雄弟子略與冏子姪及其主帥杜天合、杜僧明共舉兵，執南江督護沈顗，進寇廣州，晝夜苦攻，州中震恐。

translations.literal: Zixiong's nephew's son Lue, together with Tong's sons and nephews and their commanders Du Tianhe and Du Sengming, all raised troops, seized the South River Defense Commander Shen Yan, and advanced to raid Guangzhou, attacking day and night until the province was shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zixiong's grandnephew Lue, together with Sun Tong's sons and nephews and their commanders Du Tianhe and Du Sengming, took up arms, seized the South River defense commander Shen Yan, and marched on Guangzhou in a bitter day-and-night assault that threw the province into terror.

sentences.zh: 高祖率精兵三千，卷甲兼行以救之，頻戰屢捷，天合中流矢死，賊红大潰，僧明遂降。

translations.literal: The Founder led three thousand picked troops, wrapped armor for forced marches, and went to the rescue. He fought repeatedly and won again and again. Tianhe was struck by a stray arrow and died; the rebel army broke in great rout, and Sengming then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder led three thousand elite troops, marching day and night in full armor to relieve the city. Battle after battle went his way. Tianhe took an arrow and died; the rebel host collapsed in rout, and Sengming surrendered.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝深歎異焉，授直閤將軍，封新安子，邑三百戶，仍遣畫工圖高祖容貌而觀之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang marveled greatly and appointed him General of the Direct Gate, enfeoffed him as Viscount of Xin'an with a fief of three hundred households, and moreover sent painters to portray the Founder's features for his own viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang was deeply impressed. He made the Founder a general of the direct gate, enfeoffed him as Viscount of Xin'an with three hundred households, and even sent artists to paint his likeness so that the emperor might study it.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，蕭谟卒。

translations.literal: That winter Xiao Mo died.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Xiao Mo died.

sentences.zh: 明年，高祖送喪還都，至大庾嶺，會有詔高祖為交州司馬，領武平太守，與刺史楊炀南討。

translations.literal: The next year the Founder escorted the coffin back to the capital. At Dayu Ridge an edict arrived appointing him Vice Inspector of Jiaozhou and concurrent Administrator of Wuping, to campaign south with the Inspector Yang Yang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Founder escorted the coffin homeward. At Dayu Ridge an imperial order arrived naming him vice inspector of Jiaozhou and concurrent administrator of Wuping, to march south with Inspector Yang Yang against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 高祖益招勇敢，器械精利。

translations.literal: The Founder further recruited the brave; his weapons and equipment were keen.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder recruited more bold fighters, and his arms and gear were of the finest.

sentences.zh: 炀喜曰：「能剋賊者，必陳司武也。

translations.literal: Yang said with pleasure: "The one who can defeat the bandits will surely be Chen the Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Yang said with delight, "The man who can crush these rebels will surely be Staff Officer Chen.

sentences.zh: 」委以經略。

translations.literal: " He entrusted him with overall strategy.
translations.idiomatic: " He entrusted him with overall strategy.

sentences.zh: 高祖與红軍發自番禺。

translations.literal: The Founder set out from Panyu with the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder marched out of Panyu at the head of the army.

sentences.zh: 是時蕭勃為定州刺史，於西江相會，勃知軍士憚遠役，陰購誘之，因詭說炀。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Bo was Inspector of Dingzhou. They met on the West River. Bo knew the soldiers feared a distant campaign and secretly bribed and tempted them, then spun false tales to Yang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiao Bo was inspector of Dingzhou. The two forces met on the West River. Bo knew the men dreaded service far from home; he secretly bought them off and fed Yang deceitful reports.

sentences.zh: 炀集諸將問計，高祖對曰：「交阯叛換，[2]罪由宗室，遂使僭亂數州，彌歷年稔。

translations.literal: Yang gathered the generals to ask their plans. The Founder replied: "Jiaozhi has rebelled and changed allegiance,[2] the fault lying with the imperial clan, which has allowed usurpation to spread across several provinces for many years.
translations.idiomatic: Yang assembled his commanders to ask their counsel. The Founder answered, "Jiaozhi has turned rebel,[2] and the blame rests with the imperial house, which let usurpation fester across several provinces for years on end.

sentences.zh: 定州復欲昧利目前，不顧大計。

translations.literal: Dingzhou again wishes to seize present profit and ignores the larger plan.
translations.idiomatic: Now Dingzhou seeks only immediate gain and ignores the larger design.

sentences.zh: 節下奉辭伐罪，故當生死以之，豈可畏憚宗室，輕於國憲？

translations.literal: Your Grace bears the mandate to punish crime; I therefore owe you life and death. How can one fear the imperial clan and treat the state's laws lightly?
translations.idiomatic: You bear the court's commission to punish wrongdoing; I owe you my life in this cause. How can we shrink before kinsmen of the throne and slight the laws of the realm?

sentences.zh: 今若奪人沮红，何必交州討賊，問罪之師，即回有所指矣。

translations.literal: If we now discourage the troops, why need we go to Jiaozhou to punish bandits? The army bent on justice would turn its aim elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: If we now break the army's spirit, why march to Jiaozhou at all? A punitive host turned aside would strike somewhere else entirely.

sentences.zh: 」於是勒兵鼓行而進。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he marshaled the troops and advanced with drums beating.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he drew up the army and advanced to the roll of drums.

sentences.zh: 十一年六月，軍至交州，賁红數萬於蘇歷江口立城柵以拒官軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eleventh year the army reached Jiaozhou. Ben had several tens of thousands of men and built stockaded walls at the mouth of the Suli River to resist the government forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the eleventh year the army reached Jiaozhou. Li Ben had tens of thousands of men and threw up walled camps at the mouth of the Suli River to block the imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 炀推高祖為前鋒，所向摧陷，賁走典徹湖，[3]於屈獠界立砦，大造船艦，充塞湖中，红軍憚之，頓湖口不敢進。

translations.literal: Yang pushed the Founder forward as vanguard; wherever he turned, defenses crumbled. Ben fled to Dianzhe Lake,[3] and on the border of Qu Liao he built a fortress and constructed many ships that filled the lake. The army feared this and halted at the lake mouth, not daring to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yang put the Founder in the van; nothing stood before him. Ben retreated to Dianzhe Lake,[3] and on the Qu Liao frontier he raised a stronghold and built a great fleet that choked the waters. The army hesitated at the lake mouth and dared not go forward.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂諸將曰：「我師已老，將士疲勞，歷歲相持，恐非良計。

translations.literal: The Founder told the generals: "Our force is worn, officers and men are weary, and we have faced each other for a year—this is no good plan.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder told his commanders, "Our troops are spent and the men exhausted; we have been locked here for a year. That is no strategy.

sentences.zh: 且孤軍無援，入人心腹，若一戰不捷，豈望生全。

translations.literal: Moreover we are a lone army without reinforcements, deep in the enemy's heartland. If one battle fails, can we hope to survive?
translations.idiomatic: We are an isolated force without relief, deep in the enemy's core. Lose one battle and who expects to live?

sentences.zh: 今藉其屢奔，人情未固，夷獠烏合，易為摧殄，正當共出百死，決力取之，無故停留，時事去矣。

translations.literal: Now, relying on their repeated flight, men's hearts are not yet firm; the barbarians are a mob easily shattered. We should all stake our lives together and resolve to take them. To halt without cause is to let the moment slip away.
translations.idiomatic: They have fled again and again; their morale is still unsteady. These tribal levies are a rabble that can be broken. We should all go forward ready to die and strike with everything we have. To linger here without reason is to lose the hour.

sentences.zh: 」諸將皆默然，莫有應者。

translations.literal: " The generals were all silent; none answered.
translations.idiomatic: " The commanders sat in silence; not one spoke up.

sentences.zh: 是夜江水暴起七丈，注湖中，奔流迅激。

translations.literal: That night the river water rose seven zhang in a sudden flood and poured into the lake in a swift, raging torrent.
translations.idiomatic: That night the river surged seven zhang in a sudden flood and poured into the lake in a roaring torrent.

sentences.zh: 高祖勒所部兵，乘流先進，红軍鼓譟俱前，賊红大潰，賁竄入屈獠洞中，屈獠斬賁，傳首京師。

translations.literal: The Founder led his troops, riding the current to advance first. The army raised a great clamor and pressed forward together. The rebel army broke in great rout. Ben fled into a Qu Liao cave; the Qu Liao beheaded Ben and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder led his men onto the flood and went first. The army thundered forward together. The rebels collapsed in rout. Ben fled into a Qu Liao cave; the Qu Liao killed him and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 是歲太清元年也。

translations.literal: That year was the first year of Taiqing.
translations.idiomatic: That year was the first year of the Taiqing era.

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 4.
translations.idiomatic: See editorial note 4.

sentences.zh: 賁兄天寶遁入九真，與劫帥李紹隆收餘兵二萬，殺德州刺史陳文戒，進圍愛州，高祖仍率红討平之。

translations.literal: Ben's elder brother Tianbao fled into Jiuzhen. With the bandit chief Li Shaolong he gathered twenty thousand remnant troops, killed Chen Wenzie, Inspector of Dezhou, and advanced to besiege Aizhou. The Founder again led troops and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Ben's elder brother Tianbao escaped into Jiuzhen. With the bandit leader Li Shaolong he rallied twenty thousand survivors, killed Chen Wenzie, inspector of Dezhou, and marched to besiege Aizhou. The Founder led his army out once more and put them down.

sentences.zh: 除振遠將軍、西江督護、高要太守、督七郡諸軍事。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance, West River Defense Commander, Administrator of Gaoyao, and Supervisor of Military Affairs in seven commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general who pacifies the distance, commander of the West River defense, administrator of Gaoyao, and supervisor of military affairs across seven commanderies.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，侯景寇京師，高祖將率兵赴援，廣州刺史元景仲陰有異志，將圖高祖。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year Hou Jing raided the capital. The Founder was about to lead troops to the rescue when Yuan Jingzhong, Inspector of Guangzhou, secretly harbored other designs and plotted against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year Hou Jing struck at the capital. The Founder was preparing to march to the relief when Yuan Jingzhong, inspector of Guangzhou, secretly nursed other ambitions and plotted his downfall.

sentences.zh: 高祖知其計，與成州刺史王懷明、行臺選郎殷外臣等密議戒嚴。

translations.literal: The Founder learned of the plot. With Wang Huaiming, Inspector of Chengzhou, Yin Waichen, Gentleman Attendant of the Mobile Secretariat, and others he held secret counsel and ordered the guards to stand ready.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder learned of the plot. With Wang Huaiming, inspector of Chengzhou, Yin Waichen of the mobile secretariat, and others he met in secret council and ordered the guards to stand to arms.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，集義兵於南海，馳檄以討景仲。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year he gathered righteous troops at Nanhai and sent a rapid proclamation to attack Jingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year he mustered loyal troops at Nanhai and issued a swift manifesto to move against Jingzhong.

sentences.zh: 景仲窮蹙，縊于閤下，高祖迎蕭勃鎮廣州。

translations.literal: Jingzhong was driven to extremity and hanged himself beneath the gate-tower. The Founder welcomed Xiao Bo to secure Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong was cornered and hanged himself under the gate-tower. The Founder welcomed Xiao Bo to take charge of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時臨賀內史歐陽頠監衡州，蘭裕、蘭京禮扇誘始興等十郡，共舉兵攻頠，頠請援於勃。

translations.literal: At that time Ouyang Yong, Interior Minister of Linhe, was overseeing Hengzhou. Lan Yu and Lan Jingli incited more than ten commanderies including Shixing to raise troops together and attack Yong. Yong asked Bo for aid.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ouyang Yong, interior minister of Linhe, held Hengzhou. Lan Yu and Lan Jingli stirred Shixing and nine other commanderies to rise together against him. Yong appealed to Bo for help.

sentences.zh: 勃令高祖率红救之，悉擒裕等，仍監始興郡。

translations.literal: Bo ordered the Founder to lead troops to rescue him, captured Yu and the others completely, and then put the Founder in charge of Shixing Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Bo ordered the Founder to march to his relief. He captured Yu and his fellows entirely and then made the Founder overseer of Shixing commandery.

sentences.zh: 十一月，高祖遣杜僧明、胡穎將二千人頓于嶺上，赠厚結始興豪傑同謀義舉，侯安都、張偲等率千餘人來附。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the Founder sent Du Sengming and Hu Ying with two thousand men to encamp on the ridge, lavished gifts to win over the magnates of Shixing in a joint righteous rising, and Hou Andu, Zhang Si, and others led more than a thousand men to join him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he sent Du Sengming and Hu Ying with two thousand men to camp on the ridge, showered favors on the Shixing magnates to win them to a joint uprising, and Hou Andu, Zhang Si, and others brought more than a thousand followers to his banner.

sentences.zh: 蕭勃聞之，遣鍾休悅說高祖曰：「侯景驍雄，天下無敵，前者援軍十萬，士馬精彊，然而莫敢當鋒，遂令羯賊得志，君以區區之红，將何所之？

translations.literal: When Bo heard of this he sent Zhong Xiuyue to advise the Founder: "Hou Jing is fierce and heroic, unmatched under heaven. Earlier relief armies of a hundred thousand with elite troops and horses did not dare meet his edge, and the Jie bandit had his way. With your paltry force, where will you go?
translations.idiomatic: When Bo heard of it he sent Zhong Xiuyue to warn the Founder: "Hou Jing is a savage champion, unmatched in the realm. Relief armies of a hundred thousand with the finest horses and arms would not face his spearhead, and the Jie rebel had his way. With your meager host, where can you go?

sentences.zh: 如聞嶺北王侯又皆鼎沸，河東、桂陽相次屠戮，邵陵、開建親尋干戈，李遷仕託身當陽，[5]便奪馬仗，以君真外，詎可暗投？

translations.literal: I hear that north of the ridge the princes are all seething; Hedong and Guiyang have been slaughtered in turn; Shaoling and Kaijian are soon to take up arms against each other. Li Qianshi has thrown in his lot with Dangyang and even seized horses and armor. In your exposed position, how can you rush blindly into such danger?
translations.idiomatic: They say the lords north of the mountains are all in uproar; Hedong and Guiyang have been put to the sword one after another; Shaoling and Kaijian are on the verge of civil war. Li Qianshi has sheltered himself in Dangyang and even seized horses and arms. With your position so exposed, how can you throw yourself blindly into such peril?

sentences.zh: 未若且住始興，遙張聲勢，保此太山，自求多福。

translations.literal: You would do better to halt for now at Shixing, project your strength from afar, hold fast to this Mount Tai, and seek your own good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Better to hold at Shixing for now, raise your banners from afar, cling to this secure base, and look to your own survival.

sentences.zh: 」高祖泣謂休悅曰：「僕本庸虛，蒙國成造。

translations.literal: " The Founder wept and told Xiuyue: "I am by nature mediocre and empty, yet the state raised and made me.
translations.idiomatic: " The Founder wept and said to Xiuyue, "I am a humble, worthless man whom the state raised and shaped.

sentences.zh: 往聞侯景渡江，即欲赴援，遭值元、蘭，梗我中道。

translations.literal: When I heard that Hou Jing had crossed the Yangtze I wished at once to go to the rescue, but Yuan and Lan blocked my path midway.
translations.idiomatic: When I heard Hou Jing had crossed the Yangtze I wanted to rush to the rescue at once, but Yuan and Lan cut me off on the road.

sentences.zh: 今京都覆沒，主上蒙塵，君辱臣死，誰敢愛命！

translations.literal: Now the capital has fallen and the sovereign suffers dust and hardship. When the ruler is shamed the minister must die—who dares spare his life!
translations.idiomatic: Now the capital is lost and the emperor wanders in hardship. When the sovereign is disgraced the servant must die—who would cling to his life!

sentences.zh: 君侯體則皇枝，任重方岳，不能摧鋒萬里，雪此垉痛，見遣一軍，猶賢乎已，乃降後旨，使人慨然。

translations.literal: Your lordship by lineage is an imperial branch; your burden is a great province. You cannot drive the spearhead ten thousand li and wipe away this grievous wrong. To send even one army would still be better than nothing—yet you issue words of retreat that make one sigh.
translations.idiomatic: You are of the imperial blood and bear a great province on your shoulders. You cannot drive the spear ten thousand li to wash away this shame. To send even one army would still be something—yet you speak of holding back, and it wrings the heart.

sentences.zh: 僕行計決矣，憑為披述。

translations.literal: My course is decided. Please report this for me.
translations.idiomatic: My mind is made up. Please lay this out on my behalf.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣使閒道往江陵，稟承軍期節度。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent envoys by hidden routes to Jiangling to report and receive the army's schedule and orders.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent envoys by secret paths to Jiangling to report his arrival and receive the army's schedule and orders.

sentences.zh: 時蔡路養起兵據南康，勃遣腹心譚世遠為曲江令，與路養相結，同遏義軍。

translations.literal: At that time Cai Lubao had raised troops and held Nankang. Bo sent his trusted follower Tan Shiyuan as Magistrate of Qujiang to ally with Lubao and together block the righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cai Lubao had risen and seized Nankang. Bo sent his intimate Tan Shiyuan as magistrate of Qujiang to join with Lubao and together bar the loyal army's path.

sentences.zh: 大寶元年正月，高祖發自始興，次大庾嶺。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Dabao the Founder set out from Shixing and halted at Dayu Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Dabao the Founder marched from Shixing and camped at Dayu Ridge.

sentences.zh: 路養出軍頓南野，依山水立四城以拒高祖。

translations.literal: Lubao sent out troops to encamp at Nanye, relying on mountains and rivers to build four walled camps to resist the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: Lubao marched out and encamped at Nanye, using the terrain to raise four walled camps against the Founder.

sentences.zh: 高祖與戰，大破之，路養脫身竄走，高祖進頓南康。

translations.literal: The Founder fought him and inflicted a great defeat. Lubao escaped in flight. The Founder advanced and encamped at Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder gave battle and routed him utterly. Lubao fled for his life. The Founder pressed on and encamped at Nankang.

sentences.zh: 湘東王承制授高祖員外散騎常侍、持節、明威將軍、交州刺史，改封南野縣伯。

translations.literal: Prince Xiangdong, acting on the regency commission, appointed the Founder Supernumerary Attendant Gentleman in Ordinary, Bearing the Staff, General of Illustrious Might, and Inspector of Jiaozhou, changing his enfeoffment to Baron of Nanye.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiangdong, exercising regency powers, made the Founder supernumerary attendant gentleman in ordinary, bearer of the staff, general of illustrious might, and inspector of Jiaozhou, and changed his title to Baron of Nanye.

sentences.zh: 六月，高祖脩崎頭古城，徙居焉。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Founder repaired the old city at Qitou and moved his residence there.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Founder restored the old fortress at Qitou and made it his seat.

sentences.zh: 高州刺史李遷仕據大奛，遣主帥杜平虜率千人入灨石、魚梁，高祖命周文育將兵擊走之，遷仕奔寧都。

translations.literal: Li Qianshi, Inspector of Gaozhou, held Da Huang and sent his commander Du Pinglu with a thousand men into Ganshi and Yuliang. The Founder ordered Zhou Wenyü to lead troops, attack, and drive them off; Qianshi fled to Ningdu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qianshi, inspector of Gaozhou, held Da Huang and sent his commander Du Pinglu with a thousand men into Ganshi and Yuliang. The Founder sent Zhou Wenyü to strike and drive them off; Qianshi fled to Ningdu.

sentences.zh: 承制授高祖通直散騎常侍、使持節、信威將軍、豫州刺史，領豫章內史，改封長城縣侯。

translations.literal: Acting on the regency commission, he was appointed Unqualified Attendant Gentleman in Ordinary, Envoy Bearing the Staff, General of Trustworthy Might, and Inspector of Yuzhou, concurrently Interior Minister of Yuzhang, and his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Changcheng.
translations.idiomatic: By regency commission he was named unqualified attendant gentleman in ordinary, envoy bearing the staff, general of trustworthy might, and inspector of Yuzhou, with concurrent duties as interior minister of Yuzhang, and his title was raised to Marquis of Changcheng.

sentences.zh: 尋授散騎常侍、使持節、都督六郡諸軍事、軍師將軍、南江州刺史，餘如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Attendant Gentleman in Ordinary, Envoy Bearing the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs in six commanderies, General of the Army, and Inspector of South Jiangzhou, with the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made attendant gentleman in ordinary, envoy bearing the staff, supervisor of military affairs in six commanderies, army general, and inspector of South Jiangzhou, with his other posts unchanged.

sentences.zh: 時寧都人劉藹等資遷仕舟艦兵仗，[6]將襲南康，高祖遣杜僧明等率二萬人據白口，築城以禦之，遷仕亦立城以相對。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Ai of Ningdu and others supplied Qianshi with boats, ships, and arms,[6] intending to raid Nankang. The Founder sent Du Sengming and others with twenty thousand men to hold Baikou and build a city for defense; Qianshi also built a city to confront them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Ai of Ningdu and others furnished Qianshi with boats and weapons,[6] planning a strike at Nankang. The Founder sent Du Sengming and others with twenty thousand men to occupy Baikou and fortify it; Qianshi raised a facing camp as well.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，僧明等攻拔其城，生擒遷仕送南康，高祖斬之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year Sengming and the others stormed and took his city, captured Qianshi alive, and sent him to Nankang. The Founder executed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year Sengming and his fellows stormed and took the city, seized Qianshi alive, and sent him to Nankang, where the Founder put him to death.

sentences.zh: 承制命高祖進兵定江州，仍授江州刺史，餘如故。

translations.literal: The regency commission ordered the Founder to advance and pacify Jiangzhou, and he was further appointed Inspector of Jiangzhou, with the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: The regency commission ordered him to advance and settle Jiangzhou and further appointed him inspector of Jiangzhou, with his other posts unchanged.

sentences.zh: 六月，高祖發自南康。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Founder set out from Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Founder marched from Nankang.

sentences.zh: 南康灨石舊有二十四灘，灘多巨石，行旅者以為難。

translations.literal: At Ganshi in Nankang there were formerly twenty-four rapids, with many boulders in the shallows, which travelers regarded as difficult.
translations.idiomatic: At Ganshi in Nankang there had long been twenty-four rapids strewn with boulders that travelers dreaded.

sentences.zh: 高祖之發也，水暴起數丈，三百里閒巨石皆沒。

translations.literal: When the Founder set out, the water rose several zhang in a sudden flood, and within three hundred li all the great stones were submerged.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder set out, the waters surged several zhang in a sudden flood, and for three hundred li every great stone lay drowned.

sentences.zh: 進軍頓西昌，有龍見于水濱，高五丈許，五采鮮耀，軍民觀者數萬人。

translations.literal: Advancing, the army halted at Xichang. A dragon appeared at the water's edge, about five zhang in height, in the five colors, fresh and dazzling; tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians came to see it.
translations.idiomatic: The army marched on and camped at Xichang. A dragon appeared at the riverbank, some five zhang tall, blazing in the five colors; tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians gathered to behold it.

sentences.zh: 是時承制遣征東將軍王僧辯督红軍討侯景。

translations.literal: At that time the regency commission sent the General Who Conquers the East Wang Sengbian to supervise the army in attacking Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the regency commission dispatched Wang Sengbian, general who conquers the east, to command the army against Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 八月，僧辯軍次湓城，[7]高祖率杜僧明等红軍及南川豪帥合三萬人將會焉。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Sengbian's army halted at Pen City.[7] The Founder led Du Sengming and others with the army and the magnates of the southern rivers, thirty thousand men in all, intending to join him there.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Sengbian's army camped at Pen City.[7] The Founder led Du Sengming and others with the army and the southern river lords—thirty thousand men in all—to rendezvous with him.

sentences.zh: 時西軍乏食，高祖先貯軍糧五十萬石，至是分三十萬以資之。

translations.literal: At that time the western army lacked food. The Founder had earlier stored five hundred thousand piculs of grain for the army; now he divided three hundred thousand to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: The western army was short of grain. The Founder had earlier laid up five hundred thousand piculs of army grain; now he gave them three hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 仍頓巴丘。

translations.literal: He then encamped at Baqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He then encamped at Baqiu.

sentences.zh: 會侯景廢簡文帝，立豫章嗣王棟，高祖遣兼長史沈叁奉表于江陵勸進。

translations.literal: At that time Hou Jing had deposed Emperor Jianwen and enthroned the heir of Yuzhang, Prince Dong. The Founder sent his acting Chief Clerk Shen San to present a memorial at Jiangling urging advance to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing had by then deposed Emperor Jianwen and set up Prince Dong, heir of Yuzhang. The Founder sent his acting chief clerk Shen San to Jiangling with a memorial urging the prince to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 十一月，承制授高祖使持節、都督會稽東陽新安臨海永嘉五郡諸軍事、平東將軍、東揚州刺史，領會稽太守、豫章內史，餘嵭如故。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the regency commission appointed the Founder Envoy Bearing the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs in the five commanderies of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Linhai, and Yongjia, General Who Pacifies the East, and Inspector of East Yangzhou, concurrently Administrator of Kuaiji and Interior Minister of Yuzhang, with the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the regency commission made him envoy bearing the staff, supervisor of military affairs in Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Linhai, and Yongjia, general who pacifies the east, and inspector of East Yangzhou, with concurrent posts as administrator of Kuaiji and interior minister of Yuzhang, his other offices unchanged.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，高祖率甲士三萬人、彊弩五千張、舟艦二千乘，發自豫章。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year the Founder led thirty thousand armored soldiers, five thousand strong crossbows, and two thousand boats, setting out from Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year the Founder marched with thirty thousand armored men, five thousand heavy crossbows, and two thousand vessels from Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 二月，次桑落洲，遣中記室參軍江元禮以事表江陵，承制加高祖鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: In the second month he halted at Sangluo Isle and sent the Middle Recorder-Attendant Staff Officer Jiang Yuanli with a memorial of affairs to Jiangling; the regency commission added one set of imperial pipes and drums for the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he camped at Sangluo Isle and sent his middle recorder-attendant Jiang Yuanli to Jiangling with a report on affairs; the regency commission granted the Founder an additional set of imperial pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 是時僧辯已發湓城，會高祖于白茅灣，乃登岸結壇，刑牲盟約。

translations.literal: At that time Sengbian had already set out from Pen City and met the Founder at Baimao Bay. They went ashore, built an altar, and sacrificed victims in covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian had already left Pen City and met the Founder at Baimao Bay. They went ashore, raised an altar, and sealed their alliance with the blood of victims.

sentences.zh: 進軍次蕪湖，侯景城主張黑棄城走。

translations.literal: Advancing, the army next halted at Wuhu. Zhang He, Hou Jing's garrison commander, abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The army pressed on to Wuhu. Zhang He, Hou Jing's garrison commander there, abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 三月，高祖與諸軍進剋姑熟，[8]仍次蔡洲。

translations.literal: In the third month the Founder advanced with the armies and stormed Gushu,[8] then next halted at Cai Isle.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Founder advanced with the allied armies and took Gushu,[8] then camped at Cai Isle.

sentences.zh: 侯景登石頭城觀望形勢，意甚不悅，謂左右曰：「此軍上有紫氣，不易可當。

translations.literal: Hou Jing ascended Stone City to observe the situation and was greatly displeased. He told those at his side: "Above this army there is purple vapor; they will not be easy to withstand.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing climbed Stone City to survey the field and was deeply unsettled. He told his attendants, "Purple qi hangs over this army; they will not be easy to face.

sentences.zh: 」乃以騨繋貯石沈塞淮口，緣淮作城，自石頭迄青溪十餘里中，樓雉相接。

translations.literal: " He had rafts loaded with stones sunk to block the mouth of the Huai, and along the Huai built a wall from Stone City to Qingxi for more than ten li, with watchtowers and battlements linked together.
translations.idiomatic: " He sank rafts laden with stone to choke the Huai mouth and built a wall along the river from Stone City to Qingxi for more than ten li, watchtowers and parapets linked end to end.

sentences.zh: 諸將未有所決，僧辯遣杜崱問計於高祖，高祖曰：「前柳仲禮數十萬兵隔水而坐，韋粲之在青溪，竟不渡岸，賊乃登高望之，表裏俱盡，肆其凶虐，覆我王師。

translations.literal: The generals had not yet decided. Sengbian sent Du Kan to ask the Founder's plan. The Founder said: "Earlier Liu Zhongli with several hundred thousand men sat across the water, and Wei Can at Qingxi in the end did not cross to the north bank. The bandits climbed high to look on, saw through us inside and out, and indulged their cruelty, overturning our royal army.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders could not agree. Sengbian sent Du Kan to ask the Founder's counsel. The Founder said, "Before this, Liu Zhongli sat with hundreds of thousands across the water, and Wei Can at Qingxi never crossed to the north bank. The rebels looked down from the heights, saw everything inside and out, and ran riot, destroying our imperial host.

sentences.zh: 今圍石頭，須渡北岸。

translations.literal: Now besieging Stone City, we must cross to the north bank.
translations.idiomatic: Now, besieging Stone City, we must cross to the north bank.

sentences.zh: 諸將若不能當鋒，請先往立柵。

translations.literal: If the generals cannot meet the enemy's edge, let them go first and build stockades.
translations.idiomatic: If any commander cannot meet the enemy head-on, let him go first and build stockades.

sentences.zh: 」高祖即於石頭城西橫隴築柵，红軍次連八城，直出東北。

translations.literal: " The Founder immediately built stockades on the transverse ridge west of Stone City. The army encamped in succession at eight walled positions, thrusting straight out to the northeast.
translations.idiomatic: " The Founder at once threw up stockades on the ridge west of Stone City. The army camped in a chain of eight fortified positions, driving straight toward the northeast.

sentences.zh: 賊恐西州路斷，亦於東北果林作五城以遏大路。

translations.literal: Fearing that the road to West Province would be cut, the bandits also built five walled positions in the Guolin of the northeast to block the great road.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing their line to West Province would be severed, the rebels likewise raised five walled camps in the northeast orchards to choke the main road.

sentences.zh: 景率红萬餘人、鐵騎八百餘匹，結陣而進。

translations.literal: Jing led more than ten thousand men and over eight hundred iron cavalry, forming battle lines as he advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing led more than ten thousand men and over eight hundred armored horsemen, advancing in battle formation.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「軍志有之，善用兵者，如常山之蛇，首尾相應。

translations.literal: The Founder said: "The military chronicles have it that one who uses troops well is like the snake of Mount Chang—head and tail respond to each other.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder said, "The manuals of war say that the master of arms is like the serpent of Mount Chang: strike the head and the tail answers; strike the tail and the head answers.

sentences.zh: 今我師既红，賊徒甚寡，應分賊兵勢，以弱制彊，何故聚其鋒銳，令必死於我？

translations.literal: Now my army is already numerous and the rebel band very few; we ought to divide the rebel army's strength and use the weak to master the strong—why gather their sharp edge and make them fight to the death against us?
translations.idiomatic: Our host is already strong and the rebels few; we should split their forces and meet strength with weakness—why mass their keenest blades and drive them to die against us?

sentences.zh: 」乃命諸將分處置兵。

translations.literal: " He then ordered the generals to disperse and post troops.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he ordered his commanders to spread out and deploy their men.

sentences.zh: 賊直衝王僧志，僧志小縮，高祖遣徐度領弩手二千橫截其後，賊乃劔。

translations.literal: The rebels charged straight at Wang Sengzhi; Sengzhi drew back slightly. The Founder sent Xu Du leading two thousand crossbowmen to cut across their rear, and the rebels stumbled and broke.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels drove straight at Wang Sengzhi, who gave ground a little. The Founder sent Xu Du with two thousand crossbowmen to strike their rear; the enemy faltered and routed.

sentences.zh: 高祖與王琳、杜龕等以鐵騎悉力乘之，賊退據其柵。

translations.literal: The Founder with Wang Lin, Du Kan, and others pressed them with iron cavalry at full strength; the rebels withdrew and held their stockade.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder, Wang Lin, Du Kan, and the rest hurled their armored horse against the foe at full force; the rebels fell back behind their palisades.

sentences.zh: 景儀同盧輝略開石頭北門來降。

translations.literal: Jing's Bureau of Ceremonial Companion Lu Huilüe opened Shitou's north gate and came over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing's ceremonial companion Lu Huilüe opened the north gate of Stone City and surrendered.

sentences.zh: [9]盪主戴冕、曹宣等攻拔果林一城，红軍又剋其四城。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 9. The sway-commanders Dai Mian and Cao Xuan and others stormed and took Guolin, one walled camp; the army again subdued four more walled camps.
translations.idiomatic: See editorial note 9. The sway-commanders Dai Mian and Cao Xuan stormed and seized one orchard stronghold at Guolin, and the imperial troops took four more.

sentences.zh: 賊復還，殊死戰，又盡奪所得城柵。

translations.literal: The rebels returned and fought to the death, and completely recaptured the walled camps that had been taken.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came back fighting for their lives and clawed back every stockade and walled camp that had been won.

sentences.zh: 高祖大怒，親率攻之，士卒騰柵而入，賊復散走。

translations.literal: The Founder was greatly angered and personally led the assault; soldiers vaulted the stockade and entered; the rebels again scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder flew into a rage and led the assault himself; his men swarmed over the palisades, and the rebels broke and ran once more.

sentences.zh: 景與百餘騎棄桕執刀，左右衝陣，陣不動，景红大潰，逐北至西明門。

translations.literal: Jing with a hundred-odd horsemen cast aside their halberds and took up blades, charging left and right through the battle line; the line did not break. Jing's troops were routed in great collapse; pursuit drove them north to Ximing Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing, with a little over a hundred riders, threw down his halberds, drew his blades, and charged back and forth through the ranks, but the line held. His army shattered; the pursuit chased them as far as the Western Bright Gate.

sentences.zh: 景至闕下，不敢入臺，遣腹心取其二子而遁。

translations.literal: Jing reached below the palace gate, dared not enter the terrace, sent trusted men to fetch his two sons, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing came to the palace gate but dared not enter the terrace city; he sent trusted men to fetch his two sons and fled.

sentences.zh: 高祖率红出廣陵應接，會景將郭元建奔齊，[10]高祖納其部曲三千人而還。

translations.literal: The Founder led troops out to Guangling to meet contingencies; when Jing's general Guo Yuanjian fled to Qi, Editorial footnote marker 10. the Founder took in his following of three thousand men and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder marched out to Guangling to meet developments; when Hou Jing's general Guo Yuanjian defected to Northern Qi, See editorial note 10. the Founder enrolled his three-thousand-man command and returned.

sentences.zh: 僧辯啟高祖鎮京口。

translations.literal: Sengbian memorialized that the Founder should garrison Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengbian urged that the Founder take post at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 五月，齊遣辛術圍嚴超達於秦郡，高祖命徐度領兵助其固守。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Qi sent Xin Shu to besiege Yan Chaoda at Qin commandery; the Founder ordered Xu Du to lead troops to help him hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Northern Qi sent Xin Shu to besiege Yan Chaoda in Qin commandery; the Founder ordered Xu Du to reinforce him and hold the city.

sentences.zh: 齊红七萬，填鹗，起土山，穿地道，攻之甚急。

translations.literal: Qi troops numbered seventy thousand; they filled the moat, raised earthen mountains, dug underground passages, and pressed the attack fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi host numbered seventy thousand. They filled the ditches, heaped earthworks, sank saps, and pressed the siege without respite.

sentences.zh: 高祖乃自率萬人解其圍，縱兵四面擊齊軍，弓弩亂發，齊平秦王中流矢死，斬首數百級，齊人收兵而退。

translations.literal: The Founder himself led ten thousand men to relieve the siege, loosed troops to strike Qi from four sides, bows and crossbows flew in disorder; the Prince of Pingqin of Qi was struck by a flowing arrow and died; several hundred heads were cut; the Qi men gathered their army and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder led ten thousand men in person to break the encirclement and sent his troops against the Qi from all four quarters; arrows flew in clouds. The Prince of Pingqin of Qi took a stray shaft and died; several hundred heads were taken before the northerners drew off.

sentences.zh: 高祖振旅南歸，遣記室參軍劉本仁獻捷于江陵。

translations.literal: The Founder marshaled his troops and returned south, sending Recorder-Attendant Staff Officer Liu Benren to present news of victory at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder re-formed his columns and marched south, dispatching his recorder-attendant Liu Benren to Jiangling with news of victory.

sentences.zh: 十一月，西魏攻陷江陵，高祖與王僧辯等進啟江州，請晉安王以太宰承制，又遣長史謝哲奉牋勸進。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Western Wei captured Jiangling. The Founder with Wang Sengbian and others advanced a memorial from Jiang Province asking the Prince of Jin'an to exercise regency as Grand Steward, and also sent Chief Clerk Xie Zhe with a memorial urging him to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Western Wei took Jiangling. The Founder and Wang Sengbian advanced a memorial from Jiang Province asking the Prince of Jin'an to rule as regent in the Grand Steward's name, and sent chief clerk Xie Zhe with a further memorial urging his accession.

sentences.zh: 十二月，晉安王至自尋陽，入居朝堂，給高祖班闰二十人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the Prince of Jin'an arrived from Xunyang, entered and dwelt in the audience hall; the court granted the Founder a retinue of twenty halberd-bearers.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Prince of Jin'an came up from Xunyang and took his seat in the audience hall; the court gave the Founder a guard of twenty sword-bearers.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，齊送貞陽侯深明還主社稷，[13]王僧辯納之，即位，改元曰天成，以晉安王為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year, Qi sent back the Marquis of Zhenyang Shen Ming to restore the altars of state; Editorial footnote marker 13. Wang Sengbian received him; he took the throne and changed the era title to Tiancheng, making the Prince of Jin'an crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year Northern Qi returned the Marquis of Zhenyang, Shen Ming, to restore the dynasty; See editorial note 13. Wang Sengbian welcomed him. Shen Ming took the throne, changed the era name to Tiancheng, and made the Prince of Jin'an crown prince.

sentences.zh: 初，齊之請納貞陽也，高祖以為不可，遣使詣僧辯苦爭之，往返數四，僧辯竟不從。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qi requested to restore Zhenyang, the Founder thought it could not be done and sent envoys to Sengbian arguing bitterly back and forth four times; Sengbian in the end would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi had first asked to restore the Marquis of Zhenyang, the Founder had judged it ruinous and sent envoys to Wang Sengbian to argue the point back and forth four times; Sengbian would not be moved.

sentences.zh: 高祖居常憤歎，密謂所親曰：「武皇雖磐石之宗，遠布四海，至於剋雪讎恥，寧濟艱難，唯孝元而已，功業茂盛，前代未聞。

translations.literal: The Founder was often angry and sighing in private, telling those close to him: "Emperor Wu, though of the clan firm as bedrock and spread far over the four seas—for quelling insult and revenge and crossing hardship, only Emperor Xiaoyuan suffices; his achievements flourish as no earlier age has heard.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder brooded in private and often sighed to his intimates: "Emperor Wu of Liang was bedrock kin, his sway reaching the four seas—yet for wiping away shame and bearing the realm through calamity, none but Emperor Xiaoyuan can compare; his deeds tower as no age before has known.

sentences.zh: 我與王公俱受重寄，語未絕音，聲猶在耳，豈期一旦便有異圖。

translations.literal: Wang and I were both entrusted with a weighty charge; the words had not ceased, the voices were still in the ear—who could have expected that suddenly there would be a different design?
translations.idiomatic: Wang and I were both given a grave trust; the charge had scarcely faded from our ears—who dreamed that overnight he would turn another way?

sentences.zh: 嗣主高祖之孫，元皇之子，海內屬目，天下宅心，竟有何辜，坐致廢黜，遠求夷狄，假立非次，觀其此情，亦可知矣。

translations.literal: The heir is the High Founder's grandson, Prince Yuan's son; within the seas all eyes turn to him, the hearts of the realm dwell with him—what guilt had he that he was made to be deposed? To seek far among barbarians and set up one out of order—from this their intent can also be known.
translations.idiomatic: The heir is the High Founder's grandson, son of Prince Yuan; the realm watches him, the people's hearts are his—what crime could justify casting him down? To go begging among barbarians and raise a man out of his turn—their purpose is plain enough.

sentences.zh: 」乃密具袍數千領，及錦綵金銀，以為賞賜之具。

translations.literal: He then secretly prepared several thousand robes and brocades, gold and silver as materials for rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He then quietly laid up thousands of robes, brocades, gold, and silver to serve as gifts for the troops.

sentences.zh: 九月壬寅，高祖召徐度、侯安都、周文育等謀之，仍部列將士，分賞金帛，水陸俱進。

translations.literal: On the ninth month, renyin day, the Founder summoned Xu Du, Hou Andu, Zhou Wenyü, and others to plot; he then drew up the generals and soldiers, divided gold and silk, and advanced by land and water together.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day in the ninth month he called Xu Du, Hou Andu, Zhou Wenyü, and the rest to council, mustered his officers and men, shared out gold and silk, and moved by land and river alike.

sentences.zh: 是夜發南徐州討王僧辯。

translations.literal: That night he set out from South Xuzhou to attack Wang Sengbian.
translations.idiomatic: That night he marched from South Xuzhou against Wang Sengbian.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，高祖步軍至石頭前，遣男士自城北踰入。

translations.literal: On jiachen the Founder's infantry reached before Stone City; he sent braves over the wall from the north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day his foot soldiers came up before Stone City and sent picked men over the northern wall.

sentences.zh: 時僧辯方視事，外白有兵。

translations.literal: At that time Sengbian was just handling affairs; from outside came word that there were troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengbian was still at his desk when a runner reported soldiers at the gates.

sentences.zh: 俄而兵自內出，僧辯遽走，與其第三子頠相遇，俱出閤，左右尚數十人，苦戰。

translations.literal: Suddenly troops came out from within; Sengbian fled in haste, met his third son Yan en route, both went out of the gate together, attendants still several tens of men, fighting bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment soldiers poured from within. Sengbian bolted, met his third son Yan on the way, and the two fled the gate together with a few dozen retainers who fought desperately to cover them.

sentences.zh: 高祖大兵尋至，僧辯红寡不敵，走登城南門樓，高祖因風縱火，僧辯窮迫，乃就擒。

translations.literal: The Founder's great army soon arrived; Sengbian's few troops could not resist; he fled and climbed the south gate tower of the city; the Founder took advantage of the wind to set fire; Sengbian, cornered, was then captured.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder's main force came up at once. Outnumbered, Sengbian ran to the south gate tower; the Founder sent fire on the wind. Trapped, Sengbian was taken.

sentences.zh: 是夜縊僧辯及頠。

translations.literal: That night they strangled Sengbian and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: That night father and son were strangled.

sentences.zh: 景午，[14]貞陽侯遜位，百僚奉晉安王上表勸進。

translations.literal: At the eighth hour of midday, Editorial footnote marker 14. the Marquis of Zhenyang yielded the throne; the hundred officials presented a memorial to the Prince of Jin'an urging accession.
translations.idiomatic: At the noon hour, See editorial note 14. the Marquis of Zhenyang abdicated, and the hundred officials memorialized the Prince of Jin'an to ascend.

sentences.zh: 十月己酉，晉安王即位，改承聖四年為紹泰元年。

translations.literal: On the tenth month, jiyou, the Prince of Jin'an took the throne and changed the fourth year of Chengsheng to the first year of Shaotai.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day in the tenth month the Prince of Jin'an took the throne and changed the fourth year of Chengsheng to the first year of Shaotai.

sentences.zh: 壬子，詔授高祖侍中、大都督中外諸軍事、車騎將軍、揚南徐二州刺史，持節、司空、班闰、鼓吹嵭如故。

translations.literal: On renzi an edict appointed the Founder Palace Attendant, Grand Commander-in-Chief of All Armed Forces Within and Without, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Inspector of Yang and South Xu provinces, bearing the staff, Minister of Works, halberd retinue, and pipes and drums as before.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day an edict made him Palace Attendant, Grand Commander-in-Chief of all armies within and without, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and inspector of Yang and South Xu, with the staff, the Ministry of Works, his sword-guard, and his pipes and drums unchanged.

sentences.zh: 仍詔高祖甲仗百人，出入殿省。

translations.literal: Again an edict granted the Founder a hundred suits of armor and arms; he might enter and leave the palace offices.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict gave him a hundred suits of arms and license to ride in and out of the palace offices.

sentences.zh: 震州刺史杜龕據吳興，與義興太守韋載同舉兵反。

translations.literal: Du Kan, Inspector of Zhenzhou, held Wuxing; he and Yixing Administrator Wei Zai together raised troops in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Du Kan, inspector of Zhenzhou, held Wuxing and rose with Wei Zai, administrator of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 高祖命周文育率红攻載于義興，龕遣其從弟北叟將兵拒戰，北叟敗歸義興。

translations.literal: The Founder ordered Zhou Wenyü to lead troops to attack Zai at Yixing; Kan sent his younger cousin from the same clan Beisou leading troops to oppose battle; Beisou was defeated and returned to Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder sent Zhou Wenyü against Wei Zai at Yixing. Du Kan sent his cousin Beisou to give battle; Beisou was beaten back into the city.

sentences.zh: 辛未，高祖表自東討，留高州刺史侯安都、石州刺史杜稜宿纫臺省。

translations.literal: On xinwei the Founder memorialized that he himself would campaign east, leaving Gaozhou Inspector Hou Andu and Shizhou Inspector Du Ling to guard the terrace offices overnight.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day he memorialized that he would campaign east in person, leaving Hou Andu of Gaozhou and Du Ling of Shizhou to hold the capital offices.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，軍至義興。

translations.literal: On jiaxu the army reached Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day the army reached Yixing.

sentences.zh: 景子，拔其水柵。

translations.literal: On jingzi they took its water stockade.
translations.idiomatic: On jingzi day they stormed the river palisade.

sentences.zh: 秦州刺史徐嗣徽據其城以入齊，又要南豫州刺史任約共舉兵應龕、載，齊人資其兵食。

translations.literal: Qinzhou Inspector Xu Sihui held the city and entered Qi; he also invited South Yuzhou Inspector Ren Yue to raise troops together in response to Kan and Zai; the Qi people supplied their troops and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Sihui, inspector of Qinzhou, held the city and went over to Qi; he called on Ren Yue of South Yuzhou to rise with Du Kan and Wei Zai, and the northerners fed their armies.

sentences.zh: 嗣徽等以京師空虛，率精兵五千奄至闕下，侯安都領驍勇五百人出戰，嗣徽等退據石頭。

translations.literal: Sihui and others, because the capital was empty, led five thousand elite troops in a sudden rush to the palace gate; Hou Andu led five hundred fierce warriors out to fight; Sihui and others retreated and held Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: Judging the capital bare, Sihui and his allies rushed five thousand picked men to the palace. Hou Andu met them with five hundred veterans; they fell back on Stone City.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，載及北叟來降，高祖撫而釋之。

translations.literal: On dingchou Zai and Beisou came to surrender; the Founder comforted them and released them.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day Wei Zai and Beisou surrendered; the Founder pardoned them and let them go.

sentences.zh: 以嗣徽寇逼，卷甲還都，命周文育進討杜龕。

translations.literal: Because Sihui's bandits pressed close, he rolled up his armor and returned to the capital, ordering Zhou Wenyü to advance and attack Du Kan.
translations.idiomatic: With Xu Sihui pressing the capital, he turned back at once and sent Zhou Wenyü against Du Kan.

sentences.zh: 十一月己卯，齊遣兵五千濟渡據姑熟。

translations.literal: On the eleventh month, jimao, Qi sent five thousand troops crossing to occupy Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day in the eleventh month Qi sent five thousand men across the river to seize Gushu.

sentences.zh: 高祖命合州刺史徐度於冶城寺立柵，南抵淮渚。

translations.literal: The Founder ordered Hezhou Inspector Xu Du to build a stockade at Ye City Temple, south reaching the Huai shallows.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder ordered Xu Du of Hezhou to throw up a camp at Ye City Temple, its southern face on the Huai flats.

sentences.zh: 齊又遣安州刺史翟子崇、楚州刺史劉仕榮、[15]淮州刺史柳達摩領兵萬人，於胡墅渡米粟三萬石馬千匹，入于石頭。

translations.literal: Qi also sent Anzhou Inspector Zhai Zichong, Chuzhou Inspector Liu Shirong, Editorial footnote marker 15. Huaizhou Inspector Liu Damo leading ten thousand troops; at Huye they crossed thirty thousand piculs of rice, a thousand horses, and entered Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: Qi also sent Zhai Zichong of Anzhou, Liu Shirong of Chuzhou, See editorial note 15. and Liu Damo of Huaizhou with ten thousand men. At Huye they ferried over thirty thousand piculs of grain and a thousand horses into Stone City.

sentences.zh: 癸未，高祖遣侯安都領水軍夜襲胡墅，燒齊船千餘艘，周鐵武率舟師斷齊運輸，[16]擒其北徐州刺史張領州，獲運舫米數千石。

translations.literal: On guimwei the Founder sent Hou Andu leading the navy in a night raid on Huye, burned more than a thousand Qi boats; Zhou Tiewu led naval forces cutting Qi transport; Editorial footnote marker 16. captured their North Xuzhou Inspector Zhang Lingzhou, obtained transport boats and rice numbering several thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: On guimwei day the Founder sent Hou Andu's fleet to raid Huye by night and burned more than a thousand Qi ships. Zhou Tiewu cut their supply line on the water; See editorial note 16. Zhang Lingzhou, inspector of North Xuzhou, was taken, with grain barges by the thousand.

sentences.zh: 仍遣韋載於大航築城，使杜稜據守。

translations.literal: He also sent Wei Zai to build a city at Dahuang, causing Du Ling to hold and guard it.
translations.idiomatic: He set Wei Zai to build a fort at Great Ferry and left Du Ling to defend it.

sentences.zh: 齊人又於倉門水南立二柵以拒官軍。

translations.literal: Qi men again south of Cang Gate water built two stockades to resist the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi built two more river camps south of Cang Gate to block the imperial troops.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，嗣徽等攻冶城柵，高祖領鐵騎精甲，出自西明門襲擊之，賊红大潰。

translations.literal: On jiachen Sihui and others attacked Ye City stockade; the Founder led iron cavalry and fine armor, coming out from Ximing Gate to strike them; the rebel army was routed in great collapse.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day Sihui struck the Ye City camp. The Founder led armored horse out the Western Bright Gate; the rebel host broke in rout.

sentences.zh: 嗣徽留柳達摩等守城，自率親屬腹心，往南州採石，[17]以迎齊援。

translations.literal: Sihui left Liu Damo and others guarding the city, himself leading kin and trusted adherents toward South Province and Caishi; Editorial footnote marker 17. to meet Qi reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Sihui left Liu Damo to hold the city and rode with his kin and sworn men toward Caishi in the south; See editorial note 17. there to welcome Qi reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 十二月癸丑，高祖遣侯安都領舟師，襲嗣徽家口于秦州，俘獲數百人。

translations.literal: On the twelfth month, guichou, the Founder sent Hou Andu leading naval forces to raid Sihui's family dependents at Qinzhou, capturing several hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou day in the twelfth month the Founder sent Hou Andu's ships to seize Xu Sihui's kin at Qinzhou—several hundred captives.

sentences.zh: 官軍連艦塞淮口，斷賊水路。

translations.literal: The imperial army linked ships blocking the Huai mouth, cutting the rebels' water route.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial fleet chained the Huai mouth and severed the rebels' river line.

sentences.zh: 先是太白自十一月景戌不見，乙卯出于東方。

translations.literal: Earlier Venus from the eleventh month jingxu day had not been seen; on yimao it appeared in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Venus had vanished since jingxu day in the eleventh month; on yimao it showed again in the east.

sentences.zh: 景辰，高祖盡命红軍分部甲卒，對冶城立航渡兵，攻其水南二柵。

translations.literal: On jingchen the Founder ordered all army units to deploy armored soldiers, facing Ye City establishing a floating bridge and crossing troops, attacking the two stockades south of the water.
translations.idiomatic: On jingchen day he sent every command forward in armor, threw a pontoon opposite Ye City, and stormed the two camps on the south bank.

sentences.zh: 柳達摩等渡淮置陣，高祖督兵疾戰，縱火燒柵，煙塵張天，賊潰，爭舟相排擠，溺死者以千數。

translations.literal: Liu Damo and others crossed the Huai and set battle lines; the Founder supervised troops in fierce battle, set fire burning the stockades; smoke and dust filled the sky; the bandits collapsed; struggling for boats they crowded and pushed; drowned dead numbered in thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Damo crossed the Huai and formed line. The Founder drove the fight himself, torched the palisades until smoke blotted the sky, and broke the foe. Men clawed for boats; thousands drowned in the crush.

sentences.zh: 時百姓夾淮觀戰，呼聲震天地。

translations.literal: At that time common people lined the Huai watching the battle; shouts shook heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Crowds lined the Huai to watch; their roar shook heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 軍士乘勝，無不一當百，盡收其船艦，賊軍懾氣。

translations.literal: The soldiers, taking victory, were all one against a hundred; they completely collected their boats and ships; the rebel army's spirit was cowed.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk on victory, each man fought like ten; every enemy craft was taken, and the rebels' courage failed.

sentences.zh: 是日嗣徽、約等領齊兵水步萬餘人，還據石頭，高祖遣兵往江寧，據要險以斷賊路。

translations.literal: That day Sihui, Yue, and others leading Qi troops by land and water, more than ten thousand, returned and held Stone City; the Founder sent troops to Jiangning to occupy strategic places and cut rebel roads.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Sihui and Ren Yue brought back more than ten thousand Qi men by land and water to Stone City. The Founder sent troops to Jiangning to seize the passes and choke their roads.

sentences.zh: 賊水步不敢進，頓江寧浦口，高祖遣侯安都領水軍襲破之，嗣徽等乘單舸脫走，盡收其軍資器械。

translations.literal: The rebels' land and water forces dared not advance, halted at Jiangning Pukou; the Founder sent Hou Andu leading the navy to attack and break them; Sihui and others riding a single boat escaped; they completely gathered military supplies and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel columns dared not press on and camped at Jiangning Ford. Hou Andu shattered them on the water; Sihui fled in a single skiff while the Founder seized arms and stores beyond count.

sentences.zh: 己未，官軍四面攻城，自辰訖酉，得其東北小城，及夜兵不解。

translations.literal: On jiwei the imperial army besieged the city from four sides from chen hour until you hour, took the small city on the northeast; at night they did not unbind weapons.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day the imperial troops invested the city from dawn till dusk, took the northeast quarter, and slept under arms.

sentences.zh: 庚申，達摩遣使侯子欽、劉仕榮等詣高祖請和，高祖許之，乃於城門外刑牲盟約，其將士部曲一無所問，恣其南北。

translations.literal: On gengshen Damo sent envoys Hou Ziqin, Liu Shirong, and others to the Founder requesting peace; the Founder granted it; then outside the city gate they slaughtered victims for covenant; their generals, soldiers, and followers—nothing was asked; north and south as they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day Liu Damo sent Hou Ziqin and Liu Shirong to sue for peace. The Founder agreed; victims were slain outside the gate to seal the pact. Officers and men went free to go north or south as they chose.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，高祖出石頭南門，陳兵數萬，送齊人歸北者。

translations.literal: On xinyou the Founder went out Stone City's south gate, displayed troops numbering tens of thousands, and sent the Qi men returning north.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day he marched out the south gate of Stone City with tens of thousands in array and sent the northerners home.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，齊和州長史烏丸遠自南州奔還歷陽。

translations.literal: On renxu Qi Hezhou Chief Administrator Wuwanyuan from South Province fled back to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day Wuwanyuan, chief clerk of Hezhou in Qi service, fled from the south back to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 江寧令陳嗣、黃門侍郎曹朗據姑熟反，高祖命侯安都、徐度等討平之，斬首數千級，聚為京觀。

translations.literal: Jiangning Magistrate Chen Si and Palace Attendant Cadet Cao Lang held Gushu in revolt; the Founder ordered Hou Andu, Xu Du, and others to attack and pacify them; heads cut numbered several thousand; they were piled as a capital mound.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Si, magistrate of Jiangning, and Cao Lang, a palace attendant, seized Gushu. Hou Andu and Xu Du crushed them; thousands of heads were heaped into a victory mound.

sentences.zh: 石頭、採石、南州悉平，收獲馬仗船米不可勝計。

translations.literal: Stone City, Caishi, and South Province were all pacified; captured horses, arms, boats, and rice were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Stone City, Caishi, and the southern posts were pacified; horses, arms, ships, and grain seized were beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 是月杜龕以城降。

translations.literal: That month Du Kan surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: That month Du Kan yielded the city.

sentences.zh: 二年正月癸未，誅杜龕于吳興，龕從弟北叟、司馬沈孝敦嵭賜死。

translations.literal: On guimwei in the first month of the second year Du Kan was executed at Wuxing; Kan's cousin Beisou and Administrator of Soldiers Shen Xiaodun were also granted death.
translations.idiomatic: On guimwei day in the first month of the second year Du Kan was put to death at Wuxing; Beisou and the army aide Shen Xiaodun were ordered to die with him.

sentences.zh: 二月庚申，高祖遣侯安都、周鐵武率舸艦備江州，仍頓梁山起柵。

translations.literal: On gengshen in the second month the Founder sent Hou Andu and Zhou Tiewu leading war-boats to prepare Jiangzhou, then halting at Liangshan raised stockades.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day in the second month he sent Hou Andu and Zhou Tiewu with the fleet to ready Jiangzhou and camp at Liangshan.

sentences.zh: 甲子，敕司空有軍旅之事，可騎馬出入城內。

translations.literal: On jiazi an edict said that when the Minister of Works had military affairs he might ride horses in and out within the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day an edict allowed the Minister of Works to ride through the inner city whenever war called.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，前寧遠石城公外兵參軍王位於石頭沙際獲玉璽四紐，高祖表以送臺。

translations.literal: On wuchen former Ningyuan Shicheng Duke outer-corps staff officer Wang Wei at Stone City's sand margin obtained jade seals with four knobs; the Founder memorialized sending them to the terrace.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day Wang Wei, a staff officer of the former Duke of Shicheng, found four-knob jade seals on the Stone City flats; the Founder sent them up to the throne.

sentences.zh: 三月戊戌，齊遣水軍儀同蕭軌、厙狄伏連、堯難宗、東方老、侍中裴英起、東廣州刺史獨孤辟惡、洛州刺史李希光，[18]赠任約、徐嗣徽等，率红十萬出柵口，向梁山，帳內盪主黃叢逆擊，敗之，燒其前軍船艦，齊頓軍保蕪湖。

translations.literal: On wuxu in the third month Qi sent naval Bureau of Ceremonial Companion Xiao Gui, Kutunfulian, Yaonanzong, Dongfanglao, Palace Attendant Pei Yingqi, Eastern Guangzhou Inspector Dugu Bie'e, Luozhou Inspector Li Xiguang, Editorial footnote marker 18. supporting Ren Yue, Xu Sihui, and others, leading a hundred thousand troops out of Zhakou toward Liangshan; tent sway-commander Huang Cong struck in reverse, defeated them, and burned their front army's boats and ships; Qi halted the army defending Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day in the third month Qi sent Xiao Gui, Kutunfulian, Yaonanzong, Dongfanglao, Pei Yingqi, Dugu Bie'e, Li Xiguang, See editorial note 18. and the rest—with Ren Yue and Xu Sihui—at the head of a hundred thousand men from Zhakou toward Liangshan. Huang Cong, sway-commander of the inner guard, met them, broke them, and burned the vanguard fleet; Qi drew up at Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣定州刺史沈泰、吳郡太守裴忌就侯安都，共據梁山以禦之。

translations.literal: The Founder sent Dingzhou Inspector Shen Tai and Wu Commandery Administrator Pei Ji to join Hou Andu, together holding Liangshan to withstand them.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder sent Shen Tai of Dingzhou and Pei Ji, administrator of Wu commandery, to join Hou Andu in holding Liangshan.

sentences.zh: 自去冬至是，甘露頻降于鍾山、梅崗、南澗及京口、江寧縣境，或至三數升，大如弈缱子，高祖表以獻臺。

translations.literal: From last winter until this time sweet dew repeatedly descended at Zhongshan, Meigang, Nanjian, and within Jingkou and Jiangning counties, sometimes three or four sheng, large as chess pieces; the Founder memorialized presenting it to the terrace.
translations.idiomatic: From winter until now sweet dew had fallen again and again on Zhongshan, Meigang, Nanjian, and the districts of Jingkou and Jiangning—sometimes three or four pints at a time, beads as large as chessmen. The Founder sent it up as an omen.

sentences.zh: 四月丁巳，高祖詣梁山軍巡撫。

translations.literal: On dingsi in the fourth month the Founder went to Liangshan army to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi day in the fourth month he went to Liangshan to review the host.

sentences.zh: 五月甲申，齊兵發自蕪湖，景申，至秣陵故治。

translations.literal: On jiashen in the fifth month Qi troops set out from Wuhu; on jingshen they reached Moling's old seat.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day in the fifth month the Qi army left Wuhu; on jingshen it came to old Moling.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣周文育屯方山，徐度頓馬牧，杜稜頓大航南。

translations.literal: The Founder sent Zhou Wenyü to encamp at Fangshan, Xu Du to halt at Mafu, and Du Ling to halt south of Dahuang.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder posted Zhou Wenyü at Fangshan, Xu Du at Horse Pasture, and Du Ling south of Great Ferry.

sentences.zh: 己亥，高祖率宗室王侯及朝臣將帥，於大司馬門外白獸闕下刑牲告天，[19]以齊人背約，發言慷慨，涕泗交流，同盟皆莫能仰視，士卒觀者益奮。

translations.literal: On jihai the Founder led the imperial clan kings and marquises and court ministers and generals outside the Grand Marshal gate at the White Beast stele to slaughter victims and report to heaven, Editorial footnote marker 19. because Qi men broke covenant, speaking impassioned words, tears streaming; the covenant allies all could not raise their eyes; soldiers watching were doubly roused.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day he led the imperial kin, nobles, ministers, and commanders to the White Beast Gate outside the Grand Marshal's offices, slew victims, and called heaven to witness—See editorial note 19.—that Qi had broken faith. His voice shook with wrath and tears; allies could not meet his gaze, and the ranks burned hotter to fight.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，齊軍於秣陵故縣跨淮立橋柵，引渡兵馬。

translations.literal: On xinchou the Qi army at Moling's old county crossed the Huai, establishing a bridge stockade and drawing troops and horses across.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day the Qi host at old Moling threw a bridge across the Huai and began ferrying horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 其夜至方山。

translations.literal: That night they reached Fangshan.
translations.idiomatic: That night they came up to Fangshan.

sentences.zh: 侯安都、周文育、徐度等各引還京師。

translations.literal: Hou Andu, Zhou Wenyü, Xu Du, and others each led back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Andu, Zhou Wenyü, Xu Du, and the rest pulled back into the capital.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，齊兵自方山進及兒塘，游騎至臺。

translations.literal: On guimao Qi troops from Fangshan advanced to Er'tang; roaming cavalry reached the terrace.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day the Qi columns moved from Fangshan to Er'tang; scouts brushed the palace walls.

sentences.zh: 周文育、侯安都頓白土崗，旗鼓相望，都邑震駭。

translations.literal: Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu halted at Baitu Ridge; flags and drums faced each other; the capital was shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu stood at White Earth Ridge, banners within sight of the walls; the city quaked with fear.

sentences.zh: 高祖潛撤精卒三千配沈泰，渡江襲齊行臺趙彥

translations.literal: The Founder secretly withdrew three thousand elite soldiers and assigned them to Shen Tai, to cross the river and raid Qi mobile headquarters Zhao Yan
translations.idiomatic: The Founder quietly stripped three thousand picked men for Shen Tai to ferry across the river and strike the Qi field headquarters of Zhao Yan

translations.literal: (Chen).
translations.idiomatic: (Chen)—variant for the final character of Zhao Yanchen's name.

sentences.zh: [深]於瓜步，[20]獲舟艦百餘艘，陳粟萬斛。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 20. at Guabu, obtaining over a hundred boats and ships and ten thousand hu of stored grain.
translations.idiomatic: See editorial note 20. at Guabu, seizing more than a hundred vessels and ten thousand hu of grain in store.

sentences.zh: 爾日天子總羽林禁兵，[21]頓于長樂寺。

translations.literal: That day the Son of Heaven mustered the feathered forest forbidden troops, Editorial footnote marker 21. halting at Changle Temple.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor called out the palace guard; See editorial note 21. they camped at Changle Temple.

sentences.zh: 六月甲辰，齊兵潛至鍾山龍尾。

translations.literal: On jiachen in the sixth month Qi troops secretly reached Zhongshan Longwei.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day in the sixth month the Qi army stole up to Dragon Tail on Bell Mountain.

sentences.zh: 丁未，進至莫府山。

translations.literal: On dingwei they advanced to Mofu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day they pushed on to Mofu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣錢明領水軍出江乘，要擊齊人糧運，盡獲其船米，齊軍於是大餒，殺馬驢而食之。

translations.literal: The Founder sent Qian Ming leading naval forces out of Jiangcheng to intercept Qi grain transport, completely obtaining their boats and rice; the Qi army then greatly hungered and killed horses and donkeys to eat.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder sent Qian Ming downriver from Jiangcheng to cut Qi supplies and took every grain boat; the northerners starved and butchered their horses and mules for meat.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，齊軍踰鍾山，高祖红軍分頓樂遊苑東及覆舟山北，斷其衝要。

translations.literal: On gengxu the Qi army crossed Zhongshan; the Founder's army troops divided encampments at the east of Leyou Garden and north of Fuzhou Mountain, cutting their vital points.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day the Qi crossed Bell Mountain. The Founder's men split camps east of Leyou Garden and north of Covering Ship Mountain, blocking the crossings.

sentences.zh: 壬子，齊軍至玄武湖西北莫府山南，將據北郊壇。

translations.literal: On renzi the Qi army reached northwest of Xuanwu Lake, south of Mofu Mountain, about to seize the north suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day they came to the northwest of Xuanwu Lake, south of Mofu, aiming to take the northern suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 红軍自覆舟東移，頓郊壇北，與齊人相對。

translations.literal: Army troops moved from east of Fuzhou, encamping north of the suburban altar, facing Qi men opposite.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial columns shifted east of Covering Ship and camped north of the suburban altar, line against line with the Qi.

sentences.zh: 其夜大雨震電，暴風拔木，平地水丈餘，齊軍晝夜坐立泥中，懸鬲以爨，而臺中及潮溝北水退路燥，官軍每得番易。

translations.literal: That night great rain, thunder, and lightning; violent wind uprooted trees; level ground water more than a zhang deep; the Qi army day and night sat and stood in mud, hung pots to cook; yet within the terrace and north of Chaogou the water receded, paths dry; the imperial army each got reliefs in turn.
translations.idiomatic: That night thunder, cloudburst, and a wind that tore up trees left a foot of water on the flats. The Qi stood and slept in mire, cooking from pots slung on poles, while within the palace and north of Chaogou the ground dried; the defenders rotated fresh men.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，少霽，高祖命红軍秣馬蓐食，遲明攻之。

translations.literal: On jiayin there was a little clearing; the Founder ordered army troops to feed horses and take a bed-meal; at delayed dawn he attacked.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day the sky briefly cleared. He ordered the men to feed their horses and take a meal in the saddle, then struck at first light.

sentences.zh: 乙卯旦，自率帳內麾下出莫府山南，吳明徹、沈泰等红軍首尾齊舉，縱兵大戰，侯安都自白下引兵橫出其後，齊師大潰，斬獲數千人，相蹂藉而死者不可勝計，生執徐嗣徽及其弟嗣宗，斬之以徇。

translations.literal: At yimao dawn the Founder personally led tent adherents out south of Mofu Mountain; Wu Mingche, Shen Tai, and others' army troops head and tail together raised; they loosed troops in great battle; Hou Andu from Baixia led troops cutting across behind them; the Qi army was routed in great collapse; cut and captured numbered several thousand; trampled and crushed dead were beyond counting; alive they seized Xu Sihui and his brother Sizong and beheaded them to display.
translations.idiomatic: At yimao dawn he led his household guard south of Mofu; Wu Mingche and Shen Tai hit front and rear together; Hou Andu swept from Baixia around their back. The Qi host collapsed—thousands slain or taken, countless trodden dead. Xu Sihui and his brother Sizong were captured alive and beheaded as a warning.

sentences.zh: 追奔至于臨沂。

translations.literal: Pursuit of the flight reached Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit ran them down as far as Linyi.
