translations.literal: His posts as chancellor, governor of Yangzhou, and Supreme Commander Who Pacifies remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: His posts as chancellor, governor of Yangzhou, and supreme commander who pacifies remained as before.

sentences.zh: 又命陳王冕十有二旒，建天子旌旗，出警入蹕，乘金根車，駕六馬，備五時副車，置旄頭雲颍，樂舞八佾，設鍾廪宮縣。

translations.literal: He was further ordered as King of Chen to wear twelve tassels on the cap, raise the Son of Heaven's banners, clear the road when going out and on returning, ride the golden-root carriage, drive six horses, have five-season secondary carriages prepared, set yak-tail and cloud banners, music and dance of eight rows, and establish bell frames and palace suspended instruments.
translations.idiomatic: He was further ordered as king of Chen to wear twelve cap tassels, raise the Son of Heaven's banners, clear the road on exit and return, ride the golden-root carriage drawn by six horses, keep five-season secondary carriages, set yak-tail and cloud banners, music and dance of eight rows, and establish bell frames and palace instruments.

sentences.zh: 王妃、王子、王女爵命之號，陳臺百官，一依舊典。

translations.literal: The titles for the king's consort, princes, and princesses, and the hundred offices of the Chen administration—all followed the old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Titles for the king's consort, princes, and princesses, and the hundred offices of the Chen administration—all followed the old statutes.

sentences.zh: 辛未，梁帝禪位于陳，詔曰：

translations.literal: On xinwei day the Liang emperor abdicated the throne to Chen; an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day the Liang emperor abdicated to Chen; the edict said:

sentences.zh: 五運更始，三正迭代，司牧黎庶，是屬聖賢，用能經緯乾坤，彌綸區宇，大庇黔首，闡揚鴻烈。

translations.literal: The five movements begin anew, the three orthodoxies succeed one another; to shepherd the black-haired people belongs to the sage and worthy, whereby one can weave heaven and earth, cover the four quarters, greatly shelter the people, and spread the grand achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The five phases turn anew, the three calendars succeed one another; to shepherd the people belongs to the sage, who can weave heaven and earth, cover the realm, shelter the masses, and spread the grand achievement.

sentences.zh: 革晦以明，積代同軌，百王踵武，咸由此則。

translations.literal: Changing darkness to brightness, age piled upon age on the same track—hundred kings followed in martial steps, all by this rule.
translations.idiomatic: Darkness gave way to light, age after age on one track—hundred kings followed in martial steps, all by this rule.

sentences.zh: 梁德湮微，禍亂荐發，太清云始，見困長蛇，承聖之季，又罹封豕。

translations.literal: Liang virtue sank and faded; calamity and disorder arose in succession; at the beginning of Great Clarity one was trapped by the long serpent; in the season of Receiving Sagacity one again suffered the ravenous boar.
translations.idiomatic: Liang virtue sank and faded; calamity and disorder arose in succession; at the beginning of Great Clarity one was trapped by the long serpent; in the season of Receiving Sagacity one again suffered the ravenous boar.

sentences.zh: 爰至天成，重竊神器，三光亟沈，七廟乏祀，含生已泯，鼎命斯墜，我武、元之祚，有如綴旒，靜惟屯剝，夕惕載懷。

translations.literal: When it reached Heavenly Completion, the sacred vessel was again stolen; the three luminaries swiftly sank, the seven temples lacked sacrifice; living beings were already extinguished, the bronze mandate fell—my martial and primal fortune was like a dangling tassel; quietly I pondered difficulty and stripping, evening vigilance filled my breast.
translations.idiomatic: When it reached Heavenly Completion the sacred vessel was stolen again; the three lights swiftly dimmed, the seven temples went without sacrifice; living beings were spent, the bronze mandate fell—my martial and primal fortune hung like a dangling tassel; quietly I pondered ruin and stripping, and evening vigilance filled my breast.

sentences.zh: 相國陳王，有命自天，降神惟嶽，天地合德，晷曜齊明，拯社稷之橫流，提億兆之塗炭，東誅逆叛，北殲獯醜，威加四海，仁漸萬國，復張崩樂，重興絕禮，儒館聿脩，戎亭虛候，大功在舜，盛績惟禹，巍巍蕩蕩，無得而稱。

translations.literal: The Chancellor of State, King of Chen, had mandate from heaven and descending spirit from the peak; heaven and earth united in virtue, the sun-staff and stars alike bright; he saved the altars from the crosscurrent, lifted the hundred million from charcoal; east he punished rebellion, north he destroyed the Xianyun fiends; awesomeness reached the four seas, benevolence spread to the myriad states; he restored collapsed music, again raised extinct rites; Confucian halls were repaired, barbarian posts stood empty of scouts; great merit lay in Shun, splendid achievement only in Yu—vast, vast, none could name it.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor of state, king of Chen, had mandate from heaven and spirit from the sacred peak; heaven and earth shared his virtue, sun and stars burned bright with him; he saved the altars from the flood, lifted the millions from the coals; east he punished rebels, north he destroyed the Xianyun; his awesomeness filled the four seas, his kindness spread to every state; he restored fallen music and raised extinct rites; Confucian halls were repaired, barbarian posts stood empty; his merit matched Shun, his achievement only Yu—vast beyond naming.

sentences.zh: 來獻白環，豈直皇虞之世，入貢素雉，非止隆周之日。

translations.literal: White rings came as tribute—was it only in the age of august Yu? White pheasants entered tribute—not only on the exalted Zhou day.
translations.idiomatic: White rings came as tribute—was that only in the age of august Yu? White pheasants were offered—not only in exalted Zhou.

sentences.zh: 固以效珍川陸，表瑞煙雲，甘露醴泉，旦夕凝涌，嘉禾朱草，孳植郊甸。

translations.literal: Thus treasures were offered on rivers and land, omens shown in mist and cloud; sweet dew and sweet springs morning and evening welled and surged; fine grain and red grass sprouted thick in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Treasures rose from rivers and land, omens from mist and cloud; sweet dew and sweet springs welled morning and evening; fine grain and red grass sprouted thick in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 道昭於悠代，勳格於皇穹，明明上天，光華日月，革故著於玄象，代德彰於圖讖，獄訟有歸，謳个爰適，天之歷數，寔有攸在。

translations.literal: The Way was clear in distant ages, merit reached the august vault; bright, bright was high heaven, glory to sun and moon; change of the old was written in the dark signs, succession of virtue shown in the charts; lawsuits had their return, songs of praise turned this way—the heavenly succession truly had its place.
translations.idiomatic: The Way shone in distant ages, merit reached heaven; bright was high heaven, glory to sun and moon; change of the old was written in the dark signs, succession of virtue in the charts; lawsuits found their judge, songs of praise turned here—the heavenly succession truly had its lord.

sentences.zh: 朕雖庸藐，闇於古昔，永稽崇替，為日已久，敢忘列代之遺典，人祇之至願乎。

translations.literal: Though I am mediocre and small, dark on antiquity, long have I traced exaltation and replacement; how dare I forget the former dynasties' handed statutes and the utmost wish of men and spirits?
translations.idiomatic: Though I am mediocre and small, dark on antiquity, long have I traced rise and fall; how dare I forget the former dynasties' statutes and the utmost wish of men and spirits?

sentences.zh: 今便遜位別宮，敬禪于陳，一依唐、虞、宋、齊故事。

translations.literal: Now I yield the throne to a separate palace and respectfully abdicate to Chen, all following the stories of Tang and Yu, Song and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Now I yield the throne to a separate palace and respectfully abdicate to Chen, following the stories of Tang and Yu, Song and Qi.

sentences.zh: 策曰：

translations.literal: The written mandate says:
translations.idiomatic: The written mandate says:

sentences.zh: 咨爾陳王：惟昔上古，厥初生民，驪連、栗陸之前，容成、大庭之代，嵭結繩寫鳥，杳冥慌忽，故靡得而詳焉。

translations.literal: I address you, King of Chen: in high antiquity when living beings first arose, before Lilian and Lilu, in the age of Rongcheng and Great Court—when knotted cords and bird script, deep darkness and vast confusion—therefore none can detail it.
translations.idiomatic: I address you, king of Chen: in high antiquity when life first arose, before Lilian and Lilu, in the age of Rongcheng and Great Court—knotted cords and bird script, deep darkness and vast confusion—none can tell it in full.

sentences.zh: 自羲、農、軒、昊之君，陶唐、有虞之主，或垂衣而御四海，或無為而子萬姓，居之如馭朽索，去之如脫敝屣。

translations.literal: From the rulers Fuxi, Shennong, Xuanyuan, and Haohao to the masters Yaotang and Youyu—some draped robes and ruled the four seas, some through non-action made the myriad surnames their children; to hold it was like driving a rotten rope, to leave it like slipping off worn shoes.
translations.idiomatic: From Fuxi, Shennong, Xuanyuan, and Haohao to Yaotang and Youyu—some ruled the four seas with draped robes, some through non-action made the people their children; to hold the throne was like driving rotten rope, to leave it like slipping off worn shoes.

sentences.zh: 裁遇許由，便能捨帝，暫逢善卷，即以讓王。

translations.literal: Barely meeting Xu You, one could then yield the throne; briefly encountering Shan Juan, one at once made him king.
translations.idiomatic: Meet Xu You, and one could yield the throne; meet Shan Juan, and one at once made him king.

sentences.zh: 故知玄扈琁璣，非關尊貴，金根玉輅，示表君臨。

translations.literal: Thus one knows the dark terrace and jade armillary have nothing to do with honor; golden-root carriage and jade chariot show the sign of ruling.
translations.idiomatic: So the dark terrace and jade armillary have nothing to do with rank; golden-root carriage and jade chariot show the sign of sovereignty.

sentences.zh: 及南觀河渚，東沈刻璧，精華既竭，耄勤已倦，則抗首而笑，唯賢是與，访然作歌，簡能斯授，遺風餘烈，昭晰圖書。

translations.literal: When south he viewed the river islet and east he sank the carved jade, essence was exhausted and aged diligence already weary—then he raised his head and laughed, giving only to the worthy; suddenly he made a song, choosing ability and then conferring; surviving wind and remaining heat are clear in the books.
translations.idiomatic: When south he viewed the river islet and east he sank the carved jade, his essence was spent and aged toil weary—then he raised his head and laughed, giving only to the worthy; suddenly he sang, chose the able, and conferred; that surviving wind shines clear in the books.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏因循，是為故實。

translations.literal: Han and Wei followed in succession—this is the old reality.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei followed in succession—this is the old reality.

sentences.zh: 宋、齊授受，又弘斯義。

translations.literal: Song and Qi in receiving and giving again enlarged this principle.
translations.idiomatic: Song and Qi in receiving and giving again enlarged this principle.

sentences.zh: 我高祖應期撫運，握樞御宇，三后重光，祖宗齊聖。

translations.literal: Our Founder met the season and stroked the mandate, grasped the pivot and ruled the realm; the three queens again shone, ancestors together sage.
translations.idiomatic: Our Founder met the season and took the mandate, grasped the pivot and ruled the realm; the three queens shone again, ancestors together sage.

sentences.zh: 及時屬陽九，封豕荐食，西都失馭，夷狄交侵，乃臮天成，輕弄龜鼎，惵惵黔首，若崩厥角，微微皇極，[38]將甚綴旒。

translations.literal: When the time reached the yang nine, the ravenous boar repeatedly devoured, the western capital lost control, barbarians and Di invaded one another; then one usurped Heavenly Completion and lightly toyed with the bronze tripod; trembling were the black-haired people, as if corners collapsing; dim, dim the august pole, Editorial footnote marker 38. about to be more than a dangling tassel.
translations.idiomatic: When the time reached the yang nine, the ravenous boar devoured again, the western capital lost its helm, barbarians and Di invaded in turn; then one usurped Heavenly Completion and lightly toyed with the bronze tripod; the people trembled as if their corners would break; dim was the august pole, See editorial note 38. about to hang like a dangling tassel.

sentences.zh: 惟王乃聖乃神，欽明文思，二儀嵭運，四時合序，天錫智勇，人挺雄傑，珠庭日角，龍行武步，[39]爰初投袂，日夘勤王，電掃番禺，雲撤彭蠡，揃其元惡，定我京畿。

translations.literal: You alone are sage and divine, reverent, bright, cultured, and thoughtful; the two principles moved in concert, the four seasons in proper order; heaven bestowed wisdom and courage, men raised the heroic and outstanding; pearl forehead and sun corner, dragon stride and martial step, Editorial footnote marker 39. at first you flung up your sleeves, at the mao hour you aided the king; lightning swept Panyu, clouds cleared Pengli, leveled the chief villain, settled our capital region.
translations.idiomatic: You alone are sage and divine, reverent, bright, cultured, and thoughtful; the two principles moved as one, the four seasons in order; heaven gave wisdom and courage, men raised the hero; pearl brow and sun corner, dragon stride and martial step, See editorial note 39. at first you flung up your sleeves, at the mao hour you aided the king; lightning swept Panyu, clouds cleared Pengli, cut down the chief villain, settled our capital.

sentences.zh: 及王賀帝弘，貿茲冠屨，既行伊、霍，用保沖人。

translations.literal: When you received the king's felicitation and the emperor's enlargement, you traded this cap and shoes; already acting as Yi and Huo, you thereby protected the young ruler.
translations.idiomatic: When you received the king's blessing and the emperor's trust, you took this cap and shoes; already acting as Yi and Huo, you protected the young ruler.

sentences.zh: 震澤、稽陰，嵭懷叛逆，獯羯醜虜，三亂皇都，裁命偏師，二邦自殄，薄伐獫狁，六戎盡殪。

translations.literal: Zhenze and Kuaiji all harbored rebellion; Xianyun and Jie, ugly barbarians, thrice disturbed the imperial capital; barely ordering a partial army, the two regions destroyed themselves; a light campaign against the Xianyun, the six Rong all exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenze and Kuaiji all harbored rebellion; Xianyun and Jie, foul barbarians, thrice disturbed the capital; with a partial host alone the two regions destroyed themselves; a light strike at the Xianyun, the six Rong all wiped out.

sentences.zh: 嶺南叛渙，湘、郢結連，賊帥既擒，凶渠傳首，[40]用能百揆時序，四門允穆，無思不服，無遠不屆，上達穹昊，下漏深泉，[41]蛟魚嵭見，謳歌攸屬。

translations.literal: Lingnan rebelled and scattered, Xiang and Ying joined in alliance; the bandit chief was already taken, the vicious chieftain's head sent; Editorial footnote marker 40. thereby the hundred offices were timely in order, the four gates truly harmonious; none thought but submitted, none far but reached; above it reached the vaulted sky, below it leaked the deep springs; Editorial footnote marker 41. dragons and fish all appeared, songs of praise turned to you.
translations.idiomatic: Lingnan rebelled and scattered, Xiang and Ying joined in league; the bandit chief was taken, the vicious chieftain's head delivered; See editorial note 40. the hundred offices kept their seasons, the four gates stood in harmony; none but submitted, none so far they did not come; above it reached heaven, below the deep springs; See editorial note 41. dragons and fish all appeared, songs of praise turned to you.

sentences.zh: 況乎長彗橫天，已徵布新之兆，璧日斯既，寔表更姓之符。

translations.literal: How much more when the long comet lay across heaven—already a sign of spreading the new; the jade sun already eclipsed—truly a token of changing the surname.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when the long comet crossed heaven—already a sign of the new order; the jade sun eclipsed—truly a token of changing the surname.

sentences.zh: 是以始創義師，紫雲曜彩，肇惟尊主，黃龍負舟。

translations.literal: Therefore at first founding the righteous army, purple clouds shone in splendor; at first honoring the lord, the yellow dragon bore the boat.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore at first founding the righteous army, purple clouds shone; at first honoring the lord, the yellow dragon bore the boat.

sentences.zh: 楛矢素翬，梯山以至，白環玉玦，慕德而臻。

translations.literal: With blunt arrows and white pheasant tail-feathers, they climbed mountains to arrive; with white rings and jade disks, they came admiring virtue.
translations.idiomatic: With blunt arrows and white pheasant feathers they climbed mountains to come; with white rings and jade disks they arrived admiring virtue.

sentences.zh: 若夫安國字萌，本因萬物之志，時乘御

translations.literal: As for securing the state and nurturing the people, fundamentally it follows the will of the myriad things; timely riding and governing
translations.idiomatic: To secure the realm and cherish the people rests on the will of all under Heaven; to ride the times and steer the state

translations.literal: (bian)
translations.idiomatic: (bian)

sentences.zh: [宇]，[42]良會樂推之心。

translations.literal: [Yu], Editorial footnote marker 42. a heart meeting at the right moment for joyous yielding.
translations.idiomatic: [Yu], See editorial note 42. the heart of the age ready to yield the throne in glad accord.

sentences.zh: 七百無常期，皇王非一族，昔木德既季，而傳祚于我有梁，天之歷數，允集明哲。

translations.literal: Seven hundred years have no fixed term; kings and emperors are not of one clan. Formerly when the Wood Virtue had reached its end, the mandate passed to our Liang; Heaven's sequence truly gathers upon the wise and clear.
translations.idiomatic: Seven hundred years know no fixed span, and royal lines are not one house. When the Wood Virtue waned, the mandate came to our Liang; Heaven's count now settles on the wise.

sentences.zh: 式遵前典，廣詢戝議，王公卿尹，莫不攸屬，敬從人祇之願，授帝位于爾躬。

translations.literal: Following the former canon, broadly consulting collective deliberation, kings, dukes, ministers, and prefects—none failed to attach themselves; respectfully following the wish of human spirits, we confer the imperial seat upon your person.
translations.idiomatic: In accord with ancient precedent, after wide counsel among lords and ministers, all attached to this course; honoring the people's wish, we place the imperial throne in your hands.

sentences.zh: 四海困窮，天祿永終，王其允執厥中，軌儀前式，以副溥天之望！

translations.literal: The four seas are impoverished and exhausted; Heaven's bounty ends forever. O King, earnestly hold the center, follow the models of old, to fulfill the hope of all beneath Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: The realm is spent and Heaven's favor has run its course. Hold the Mean, follow the old patterns, and answer what all under Heaven expects of you!

sentences.zh: 禋祀上帝，時膺大禮，永固洪業，豈不盛歟！

translations.literal: In suburban sacrifice to the Supreme Lord, timely receive the great rites, forever secure the vast enterprise—is it not magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to Heaven, receive the great rites in season, and make the great enterprise endure—what glory could be greater!

sentences.zh: 又璽書曰：

translations.literal: An edict by imperial seal also said:
translations.idiomatic: A sealed edict also said:

sentences.zh: 君子者自昭明德，達人者先天弗違，故能進退咸亨，動靜元吉。

translations.literal: The gentleman brightens his own virtue; the man of attainment is ahead of Heaven and does not violate it—therefore in advance and retreat all is penetrating, in movement and stillness primordially auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman makes his virtue shine; the sage anticipates Heaven and does not oppose it—so whether he advances or withdraws all goes well, and in action or repose he is fundamentally blessed.

sentences.zh: 朕雖蒙寡，庶乎景行。

translations.literal: Though We are shallow and few, We are perhaps not far from that lofty conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Though We are dull and slight, We may yet approach that high example.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why so?

sentences.zh: 三才剖判，九有區分，情性相乖，亂離云起，是以建彼司牧，推乎聖賢，授受者任其時來，皇王者本非一族，人謀是與，屈己從萬物之心，天意斯歸，鞠躬奉百靈之命。

translations.literal: When the three powers were divided and the nine domains distinguished, natures and dispositions diverged and disorder rose like clouds—therefore they established those who tend the people and promoted the sage and worthy; those who received and yielded took office as the time came; kings and emperors by origin were not one clan; human counsel agreed; one bent oneself to follow the heart of the myriad things; Heaven's intent thus returned; one bowed the body to serve the command of the hundred spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Once heaven, earth, and man were set apart and the realm was carved into regions, hearts pulled apart and chaos spread—so rulers were appointed and sages raised up. Transfer of the mandate came when the time came; dynasties were not one bloodline. Where human counsel agreed, the throne bent to the people's will; where Heaven turned, the ruler bowed to the spirits.

sentences.zh: 謳个所往，則攘袂以膺之，菁華已竭，乃褰裳而去之。

translations.literal: Where songs of acclaim went, one rolled up one's sleeves to receive it; when the essence was spent, one lifted one's robe and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Where popular acclaim led, the ruler rolled up his sleeves and took the burden; when his virtue was spent, he gathered his robe and walked away.

sentences.zh: 昔在唐、虞，鑒于天道，舉其黎獻，授彼明哲，雖復質文殊軌，沿革不同，歷代因循，斯風靡替。

translations.literal: Formerly under Tang and Yu, taking Heaven's way as mirror, they raised the black-haired people and conferred it upon the wise and clear; though substance and pattern, writing and track differed and institutions changed with the age, through successive generations this wind never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang and Yu times, mirroring Heaven, they chose the people and gave rule to the wise; forms and rites changed from age to age, yet the custom of yielding never died out.

sentences.zh: 我大梁所以考庸太室，接禮貳宮，月正元日，受終文祖。

translations.literal: Our Great Liang therefore examined merit in the Grand Temple, received rites at the secondary palace, on the first day of the first month received the end from the civil ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Our Liang thus tested merit in the Grand Temple, received the rites at the secondary palace, and on New Year's Day took the mandate from the former sovereign.

sentences.zh: 但運不常夷，道無恆泰，山岳傾偃，河海沸騰，電目雷聲之禽，鉤爪鋸牙之獸，咀齧含生，不知紀極。

translations.literal: But fortune is not always level and the Way has no constant peace; mountains and hills toppled, rivers and seas seethed; birds with lightning eyes and thunder voices, beasts with hooked claws and saw teeth, chewed and devoured the living without knowing limit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet fortune is not always smooth and the Way not always tranquil: mountains overturned and seas boiled; monstrous birds and savage beasts devoured life without end.

sentences.zh: 二后英聖，相仍在天，六夷貪狡，爭侵中國，縣王都帝，人懷干紀，一民尺土，皆非梁地。

translations.literal: The two sovereigns were heroic and sage, succeeding one another in Heaven; the six Yi were greedy and cunning and strove to invade the central land; men set up as kings and emperors harbored designs against the statutes; not one man or inch of soil was any longer Liang territory.
translations.idiomatic: Two sage emperors followed one another in Heaven, yet the six barbarians clawed at the heartland; pretenders raised banners and men nursed treason; not a man or a foot of soil truly remained Liang ground.

sentences.zh: 朕以不造，幼罹閔凶，仰憑衡佐，亟移年序。

translations.literal: We, through misfortune, in youth met with bereavement, relying upward on balancing assistants; years swiftly shifted.
translations.idiomatic: We, ill-fated, lost our father young and leaned on regents while the years hurried by.

sentences.zh: 周成、漢惠，邈矣無階，惟是童蒙，必貽顛晋。

translations.literal: King Cheng of Zhou and Emperor Hui of Han—how far off, without a stair! Only this childish innocence was bound to bring downfall.
translations.idiomatic: King Cheng of Zhou and Emperor Hui of Han are far beyond reach; this childish rule could only invite ruin.

sentences.zh: 若使時無聖哲，世靡艱難，猶當高蹈於滄洲，自求於泰伯者矣。

translations.literal: If the age had lacked a sage and the world had not known hardship, We would still have strode high on the blue isles and sought for Ourselves the path of Taibo.
translations.idiomatic: Had there been no sage and no calamity, We would still have withdrawn to the marshes and sought Taibo's way of yielding.

sentences.zh: 惟王應期誕秀，開籙握圖，性道故其難聞，嘉庸已其被物，乾行同其燾覆，日御比其貞明，登承聖於復禹之功，樹鞠子於興周之業，滅陸渾於伊、洛，殲驪戎於鎬京，大小二震之驍徒，東南兩越之勍寇，遽行天討，無遺神策。

translations.literal: Only the King answered the age and was born outstanding, opened the register and grasped the chart; the Way and its teaching are therefore hard to hear of, fine merit already covers things; the Qian movement matches its sheltering canopy, the sun chariot compares to its steadfast brightness; he ascended to receive the sage's work of restoring Yu, set up the foster son in the enterprise of raising Zhou, destroyed Luhun at Yi and Luo, annihilated the Li Rong at Haojing; the fierce troops of the two Zhens great and small, the powerful foes of the two Yues southeast and southwest—suddenly Heaven's punishment was carried out, none missed by divine strategy.
translations.idiomatic: But the King met his season, opened the mandate and held the chart; his virtue is hard to name and his merit already blankets the world. Like Heaven's canopy he shelters all; like the sun he shines steady. He took up Yu's restoration and Zhou's founding charge, crushed Luhun on the Yi and Luo and the Li Rong at Haojing, and swept the fierce hosts of the two Zhens and the strong rebels of the two Yues—Heaven's strike fell at once, nothing escaping his design.

sentences.zh: 於是祖述堯舜，憲章文武，大樂與天地同和，大禮與天地同節，鼓之以雷霆，潤之以風雨，仁霑葭葦，信及豚魚，殷牖斯空，夏臺虛設，民惟大畜，野有同人，升平頌平，無偏無黨，固以雲飛紫蓋，水躍黃龍，東伐西征，晻映川陸，榮光曖曖，已冒郊廛，甘露瀼瀼，亟流庭苑。

translations.literal: Thereupon he traced Yao and Shun and took Wen and Wu as model; great music harmonized with heaven and earth, great rites shared their seasons with heaven and earth; drummed with thunder, moistened with wind and rain; benevolence soaked the reeds, faith reached pigs and fish; the Yin window stood empty, the Xia tower was void; the people were greatly stored, in the wild there were fellows; the Ascendant Peace hymn was sung, without partiality or faction—firmly clouds flew over the purple canopy, the yellow dragon leapt in the waters; east campaign and west expedition gleamed across rivers and land; glory warmed and already overspread the suburbs; sweet dew dripped and repeatedly flowed through the palace gardens.
translations.idiomatic: He took Yao and Shun as his model and Wen and Wu as his law; music and rites matched heaven and earth; thunder drummed and rain moistened; kindness reached the humblest grass, trust even to fish and swine; prisons stood empty and towers unused; the people flourished and harmony filled the land. Clouds crowned the purple canopy and dragons leapt in the waters; his armies flashed across the realm; glory bathed the suburbs and sweet dew drenched the palace courts.

sentences.zh: 車轍馬跡，誰不率從？

translations.literal: Cart ruts and horse tracks—who did not follow?
translations.idiomatic: Cart tracks and hoofprints—who did not follow?

sentences.zh: 蟠水流沙，誰不懷德？

translations.literal: Coiling waters and flowing sands—who did not cherish virtue?
translations.idiomatic: From winding streams to shifting sands—who did not honor his virtue?

sentences.zh: 祥圖遠至，非唯赤伏之符，靈命昭然，何止黃星之氣。

translations.literal: Auspicious charts came from afar—not only the red talisman; the numinous mandate was clear—not only the yellow star's breath.
translations.idiomatic: Portents arrived from afar, not only the red talisman of Liu Bang; Heaven's mandate was plain, not only the yellow star's omen.

sentences.zh: 海口河目，賢聖之表既彰，握旄執鉞，君人之狀斯偉。

translations.literal: River mouth and river eyes—the sage's outward signs were already displayed; grasping the banner and holding the battle-axe—the ruler's form was thus grand.
translations.idiomatic: The marks of a sage showed in his face; bearing banner and axe, he had the bearing of a true king.

sentences.zh: 且自攝提無紀，孟陬殄滅，枉矢宵飛，天弧曉映，久矣夷羊之在牧，時哉蛟龍之出泉。

translations.literal: Moreover from the time Sheti lost its reckoning and Mengzou perished, the crooked arrow flew by night and the sky bow shone at dawn—long had the barbarian sheep been in the pastures; the hour had come for the flood dragon to rise from the spring.
translations.idiomatic: Since the stars lost their order and the calendar broke down, comets crossed the night sky—barbarians had long overrun the fields; the time had come for the dragon to rise from the deep.

sentences.zh: 革運之兆咸徵，惟新之符嵭集，朕所以欽若勛、華，屢回星琯。

translations.literal: Omens of a change in mandate were all manifest; tokens of renewal gathered thickly—We therefore revered Kun and Hua and repeatedly turned the star gauge.
translations.idiomatic: Every sign of a new mandate appeared; tokens of renewal gathered—so We revered the models of Yao and Shun and long hesitated before Heaven's clock.

sentences.zh: 昔者木運斯盡，予高祖受焉。

translations.literal: Formerly when the Wood cycle was spent, Our High Ancestor received it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wood mandate ended, our founder received it.

sentences.zh: 今歷去炎精，神歸樞紐，敬以火德，傳于爾陳。

translations.literal: Now the calendar has left the Fire brilliance; the spirit returns to the pivot; respectfully with the Fire Virtue We transmit it to your Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Fire mandate has run its course and the spirit returns to the center; We respectfully pass the Fire mandate to your Chen.

sentences.zh: 遠鑒前王，近謀戝辟，明靈有悅，率土同心。

translations.literal: Looking far to former kings and consulting near with the hundred lords, the bright spirits are pleased and all within the seas share one heart.
translations.idiomatic: Taking former kings as mirror and the hundred lords as counsel, the spirits approve and the realm is of one mind.

sentences.zh: 今遣使持節兼太保侍中尚書左僕射平樂亭侯王通，[43]兼太尉司徒左長史王瑒奉皇帝璽綬。

translations.literal: Now We send envoys bearing credentials: concurrently Grand Mentor, Palace Attendant, Minister of the Masters of Writing, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Marquis of Pingle Precinct Wang Tong, Editorial footnote marker 43. and concurrently Grand Commandant, Director of the Masters of Writing, Left chief clerk Wang Chang to present the imperial seal and cord.
translations.idiomatic: We now send envoys with credentials: Grand Mentor and Left Vice Director Wang Tong, See editorial note 43. and Grand Commandant chief clerk Wang Chang, to deliver the imperial seal and cord.

sentences.zh: 受終之禮，一依唐、虞故事。

translations.literal: The rites of receiving the end shall wholly follow the Tang and Yu precedents.
translations.idiomatic: The abdication rites shall follow entirely the precedent of Tang and Yu.

sentences.zh: 王其時陟元后，寧育兆民，光闡洪猷，以承昊天之休命！

translations.literal: O King, at the proper time ascend as the primary consort, nurture and rear the hundred thousand people, broadly unfold the great design, to receive the felicitous mandate of august Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: King, take the throne in due season, nurture the people, and unfold the great plan to receive Heaven's bright command!

sentences.zh: 是日梁帝遜于別宮。

translations.literal: That day the Liang Emperor yielded the throne at a separate palace.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Liang emperor abdicated to a side palace.

sentences.zh: 高祖謙讓再三，戝臣固請，乃許。

translations.literal: The Founder declined again and again; the hosts of ministers firmly pressed him, and he then assented.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder refused again and again until the ministers pressed him firmly, and then he accepted.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 新喻侯蕭谟為吳興太守 「新喻」《杜僧明傳》作「新渝」，他處亦喻渝互見。

translations.literal: Marquis of Xinyu Xiao Mo served as Administrator of Wuxing: "Xinyu" in the Biography of Du Sengming reads "Xinyu" (Yu with water radical); elsewhere Yu and Yu also appear interchangeably.
translations.idiomatic: On "Marquis of Xinyu Xiao Mo, administrator of Wuxing": the Biography of Du Sengming writes Xinyu with the water radical; the speech and water forms interchange elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 按「新喻」之「喻」本作「渝」，因渝水為名，唐天寶後相承作「喻」，詳見《唐書·地理志》及《元和郡縣志》。

translations.literal: Comment: the "Yu" of "Xinyu" was originally written "Yu" (with water), named for the Yu River; after Tianbao of Tang the form "Yu" (with speech) was used in succession—see the Treatise on Geography in the Book of Tang and the Yuanhe Commanderies and Counties Gazetteer.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Xinyu was originally written with the water radical for the Yu River; after Tang Tianbao the speech radical form became standard—see the Book of Tang geography treatise and the Yuanhe gazetteer.

sentences.zh: 「蕭谟」《杜僧明傳》作「蕭映」，他處亦谟映互見，今以谟映同字，不改歸一律。

translations.literal: "Xiao Mo" in the Biography of Du Sengming reads "Xiao Ying"; elsewhere Mo and Ying also appear interchangeably; now Mo and Ying are treated as the same character and are not normalized to one form.
translations.idiomatic: On "Xiao Mo": the Biography of Du Sengming reads Xiao Ying; Mo and Ying interchange elsewhere; the forms are treated as variants and not forced to one spelling.

sentences.zh: 交阯叛換 「叛換」各本作「叛渙」。

translations.literal: Jiaozhi rebelled and turned: "rebelled and turned" in all editions reads "rebelled and scattered."
translations.idiomatic: On "Jiaozhi rebelled and turned": all editions read rebelled and scattered.

sentences.zh: 按叛換、叛渙皆疊韻聯穂字，音同而義亦相近，本書換渙互用之處數見，後如此不悉出校記。

translations.literal: Comment: rebelled-and-turned and rebelled-and-scattered are both reduplicative binomes; the sound is the same and the sense close. Where this book uses turn and scatter interchangeably there are several instances; hereafter such cases are not all given collation notes.
translations.idiomatic: Rebelled-and-turned and rebelled-and-scattered are variant binomes of like sound and sense. The book uses turn and scatter interchangeably in several places; not every case is noted below.

sentences.zh: 賁走典徹湖 按「徹」當作「澈」。

translations.literal: Ben fled toward Dian Che Lake: comment—the character "Che" should be "Che" (clear water).
translations.idiomatic: On "Ben fled toward Dian Che Lake": Che should be Che (clear).

sentences.zh: 策陳霸先九錫文有「新昌、典澈，備履艱難」語，舊校云「『典澈』或本作『曲澈』，前有『典澈湖』，亦同」。

translations.literal: The document conferring nine bestowments on Chen Baxian has the phrase "Xinchang and Dian Che, fully treading hardship"; an old collation says "'Dian Che' may originally have read 'Qu Che,' and the earlier 'Dian Che Lake' is the same."
translations.idiomatic: The nine-bestowments text for Chen Baxian reads Xinchang and Dian Che, having fully borne hardship; old collation says Dian Che may have been Qu Che, as with Dian Che Lake above.

sentences.zh: 是舊校所見本亦作「澈」也。

translations.literal: Thus the edition seen by the old collation also read "Che."
translations.idiomatic: The edition used by the old collation also read Che.

sentences.zh: 是歲太清元年也 按《梁書·武帝紀》，李賁兵潰在中大同元年正月，其被殺則在太清二年三月。

translations.literal: That year was the first year of Taiqing: comment—according to the Annals of Emperor Wu in the Book of Liang, Li Ben's army collapsed in the first month of the first year of Zhongdatong, and he was killed in the third month of the second year of Taiqing.
translations.idiomatic: On "that year was Taiqing year 1": the Book of Liang places Li Ben's rout in Zhongdatong 1/1 and his death in Taiqing 2/3.

sentences.zh: 李遷仕託身當陽 「託」各本作「許」。

translations.literal: Li Qianshi entrusted himself to Dangyang: "entrusted" in all editions reads "promised."
translations.idiomatic: On "Li Qianshi entrusted himself to Dangyang": all editions read promised for entrusted.

sentences.zh: 殿本考證云「許」一本作「託」。

translations.literal: The Hall edition's textual verification says: in one edition "promised" reads "entrusted."
translations.idiomatic: The Hall edition notes one manuscript reads entrusted for promised.

sentences.zh: 張元濟

translations.literal: Zhang Yuanji
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuanji

sentences.zh: 〈校勘記〉

translations.literal: 〈Collation notes〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Collation notes〉

sentences.zh: 云「託」字義長。

translations.literal: says: "The character 'entrusted' is semantically superior."
translations.idiomatic: says entrusted is the better reading.

sentences.zh: 時寧都人劉藹等資遷仕舟艦兵仗 「劉藹」《杜僧明傳》、《周文育傳》並作「劉孝尚」，豈一人而異名歟？

translations.literal: At the time the people of Ningdu, Liu Ai and others, supplied Qianshi with boats, armor, and weapons: "Liu Ai" in the Biographies of Du Sengming and Zhou Wenyu both read "Liu Xiaoshang"—are they one man with different names?
translations.idiomatic: On "Liu Ai of Ningdu supplied Qianshi with ships and arms": Du Sengming's and Zhou Wenyu's biographies read Liu Xiaoshang—one person under two names?

sentences.zh: 僧辯軍次湓城 「湓」《南史·陳武帝紀》作「盆」。

translations.literal: Sengbian's army halted at Pen city: "Pen" in the Annals of Emperor Wu in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Basin."
translations.idiomatic: On "Sengbian halted at Pen city": the Southern History's Chen Wu annals read Basin.

sentences.zh: 按「湓城」或省作「盆城」，史文二字互用，後如此不悉出校記。

translations.literal: Comment: "Pen city" may be abbreviated as "Basin city"; the histories use the two graphs interchangeably—hereafter such cases are not all given collation notes.
translations.idiomatic: Pen city may be shortened to Basin city; the histories interchange the two forms—not every case is noted below.

sentences.zh: 高祖與諸軍進剋姑熟 「姑熟」北監本、汲古閣本、殿本並作「姑孰」。

translations.literal: The Founder with the various armies advanced and took Gushu: "Gushu" in the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions all read "Gushu" (with the mature graph).
translations.idiomatic: On "took Gushu": Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions write Gushu with the mature character.

sentences.zh: 按孰熟字同，史文二字亦多互見，後如此不悉出校記。

translations.literal: Comment: the graphs shu and shu are the same; the histories also often interchange the two—hereafter such cases are not all given collation notes.
translations.idiomatic: Shu and shu are the same character and often interchange in the histories—not every case is noted below.

sentences.zh: 景儀同盧輝略開石頭北門來降 「盧輝略」《梁書·侯景傳》作「盧暉略」，通鑑同。

translations.literal: Jing's Commissioner Equal to the Three Dukes Lu Huilue opened Stone City's north gate and came over: "Lu Huilue" in the Biography of Hou Jing in the Book of Liang reads "Lu Huilue"; the Comprehensive Mirror agrees.
translations.idiomatic: On "Lu Huilue opened Stone City's north gate and surrendered": the Book of Liang's Hou Jing biography and the Comprehensive Mirror read Lu Huilue.

sentences.zh: 高祖率红出廣陵應接會景將郭元建奔齊 《太平御覽》一三三引作「高祖率红出廣陵應接景將郭元建，會元建奔齊」，《冊府元龜》一八六同，文意較明，此有脫文。

translations.literal: The Founder led the red out from Guangling to meet contingencies; when Jing's general Guo Yuanjian fled to Qi: the Taiping Imperial Overview 133 quotes, "The Founder led troops out from Guangling to meet Jing's general Guo Yuanjian; when Yuanjian fled to Qi"; the Yuan Gui 186 agrees—the sense is clearer; here there is omitted text.
translations.idiomatic: On "the Founder led the red from Guangling": Taiping yulan 133 and Yuan Gui 186 read led troops to meet Guo Yuanjian, who then fled to Qi—clearer than the received text, which omits words.

sentences.zh: 湘州平 殿本考證云「梁書湘州平係承聖二年事」。

translations.literal: Xiang Province was pacified: the Hall edition's textual verification says, "The pacification of Xiang Province in the Book of Liang belongs to the affairs of the second year of Chengsheng."
translations.idiomatic: On "Xiang Province pacified": the Hall edition places this in Chengsheng year 2 in the Book of Liang.

sentences.zh: 今按《南史·陳武帝紀》繫此事於承聖二年，通鑑同，元龜一八六同。

translations.literal: Now examining the Annals of Emperor Wu in the History of the Southern Dynasties, this matter is placed in the second year of Chengsheng; the Comprehensive Mirror agrees; Yuan Gui 186 agrees.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern History and Comprehensive Mirror date the pacification of Xiang Province to Chengsheng year 2; Yuan Gui 186 agrees.

sentences.zh: 御覽一三三引「湘州平」上有「明年」二字，疑此有脫文。

translations.literal: Imperial Overview 133 quotes above "Xiang Province pacified" the two characters "next year"—suspected omitted text here.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping yulan 133 has next year before "Xiang Province pacified"—the main text may lack those words.

sentences.zh: 三年三月進高祖位司空 《梁書·元帝紀》作「四月癸酉」，通鑑同。

translations.literal: In the third year, third month, the Founder was advanced to Grand Commandant: the Annals of Emperor Yuan in the Book of Liang reads "fourth month, guiyou"; the Comprehensive Mirror agrees.
translations.idiomatic: On "year 3, month 3, advanced to Grand Commandant": the Book of Liang and Comprehensive Mirror read month 4, guiyou.

sentences.zh: 齊送貞陽侯深明還主社稷 「深明」即「淵明」，此避唐高祖諱改，後同。

translations.literal: Qi sent back the Marquis of Zhenyang Shen Ming to restore the altars of state: "Shen Ming" is "Yuan Ming"—changed to avoid the taboo of Tang Gaozu; the same below.
translations.idiomatic: On "Qi returned Marquis of Zhenyang Shen Ming": Shen Ming stands for Yuan Ming, tabooed for Tang Gaozu—the same below.

sentences.zh: 景午 即丙午。

translations.literal: Jingwu—that is, Bingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwu is Bingwu.

sentences.zh: 姚思廉避唐高祖父諱，「丙」字皆改為「景」，後如此不悉出校記。

translations.literal: Yao Silian avoided the taboo of Tang Gaozu's grandfather; the character "bing" is everywhere changed to "jing"—hereafter such cases are not all given collation notes.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Silian tabooed Tang Gaozu's grandfather and wrote jing for bing throughout—not every case is noted below.

sentences.zh: 楚州刺史劉仕榮 《南史·陳武帝紀》作「劉士榮」。

translations.literal: Chu Province Inspector Liu Shirong: the Annals of Emperor Wu in the History of the Southern Dynasties read "Liu Shirong."
translations.idiomatic: On "Chu Inspector Liu Shirong": the Southern History's Chen Wu annals read Liu Shirong.

sentences.zh: 周鐵武率舟師斷齊運輸 「周鐵武」即「周鐵虎」，此避唐高祖祖父諱改，後同。

translations.literal: Zhou Tiewu led naval forces cutting Qi transport: "Zhou Tiewu" is "Zhou Tiehu"—changed to avoid the taboo of Tang Gaozu's grandfather; the same below.
translations.idiomatic: On "Zhou Tiewu cut Qi supply lines": Tiewu is Tiehu, tabooed for Tang Gaozu's grandfather—the same below.

sentences.zh: 往南州採石 「採石」南監本、北監本、殿本作「采石」。

translations.literal: Going south to the province at Caishi: "Caishi" in the Southern Supervisory, Northern Supervisory, and Hall editions read "Caishi" (with the harvest graph).
translations.idiomatic: On "south to Caishi": Southern, Northern Supervisory, and Hall editions write Caishi with the harvest character.

sentences.zh: 按采採同字，史文二字亦多互見，後如此不悉出校記。

translations.literal: Comment: the graphs cai and cai are the same; the histories also often interchange the two—hereafter such cases are not all given collation notes.
translations.idiomatic: Cai and cai are the same character and often interchange—not every case is noted below.

sentences.zh: 洛州刺史李希光 張森楷

translations.literal: Luozhou Inspector Li Xiguang: Zhang Senkai
translations.idiomatic: On "Luozhou Inspector Li Xiguang": Zhang Senkai

sentences.zh: 〈校勘記〉

translations.literal: 〈Collation notes〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Collation notes〉

sentences.zh: 云：「北齊書高乾傳附弟季式傳，謂李希光於齊天保中為揚州刺史，與蕭軌等渡江戰沒，與此異。」

translations.literal: says: "In the Biography of Gao Gan in the Book of Northern Qi, with the attached biography of his younger brother Jishi, it states that Li Xiguang in Northern Qi Tianbao served as Yangzhou inspector and, with Xiao Gui and others, crossed the river and died in battle—this differs from here."
translations.idiomatic: says the Northern Qi biography of Gao Gan's brother Jishi makes Li Xiguang Yangzhou inspector under Tianbao, killed crossing the river with Xiao Gui—which disagrees with this passage.

sentences.zh: 於大司馬門外白獸闕下刑牲告天 「白獸闕」即「白虎闕」，此避唐諱改，後同。

translations.literal: Outside the Grand Marshal gate at the White Beast stele slaughtered victims and reported to Heaven: "White Beast stele" is "White Tiger stele"—changed to avoid Tang taboo; the same below.
translations.idiomatic: On "White Beast stele": White Beast is White Tiger, tabooed under Tang—the same below.

sentences.zh: 渡江襲齊行臺趙彥

translations.literal: Crossed the river to strike Qi Acting Commander Zhao Yan
translations.idiomatic: Crossed the river to attack Qi acting commander Zhao Yan

translations.literal: (Chen)
translations.idiomatic: (Chen)

sentences.zh: [深]於瓜步 據《南史·陳武帝紀》改。

translations.literal: [Shen] at Guabu: corrected according to the Annals of Emperor Wu in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: [Shen] at Guabu: emended per the Southern History's Chen Wu annals.

sentences.zh: 按趙彥深北齊書有傳，傳稱其本名隱，避齊廟諱，故以字行。

translations.literal: Comment: Zhao Yanshen has a biography in the Book of Northern Qi; the biography says his original name was Yin, and to avoid Qi temple taboo he went by his style.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Zhao Yanshen's Northern Qi biography says his original name was Yin; he used his style to avoid Qi temple taboo.

sentences.zh: 古人名字相應，自以作「深」為是。

translations.literal: In antiquity personal names and styles corresponded—naturally to write "Shen" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient name and style matched; Shen is the correct reading.

sentences.zh: 爾日天子總羽林禁兵 「爾日」各本作「即日」。

translations.literal: That day the Son of Heaven mustered the feathered forest forbidden troops: "that day" in all editions reads "this day."
translations.idiomatic: On "that day the emperor mustered the palace guard": all editions read this day for that day.

sentences.zh: 按爾日猶即日，字異而義同。

translations.literal: Comment: that day is the same as this day—the graphs differ but the sense is the same.
translations.idiomatic: That day and this day mean the same; only the graphs differ.

sentences.zh: 斬劉歸義徐嗣彥傅野嚢于建康市 「徐嗣彥」《梁書·敬帝紀》、《南史·陳帝紀》並作「徐嗣產」。

translations.literal: Beheaded Liu Guiyi, Xu Siyan, and Fu Yenang in the Jiankang market: "Xu Siyan" in the Annals of the Deposed Emperor in the Book of Liang and the Annals of the Chen Emperor in the History of the Southern Dynasties both read "Xu Sichan."
translations.idiomatic: On "beheaded Xu Siyan at Jiankang market": the Book of Liang's Deposed Emperor annals and the Southern History's Chen annals read Xu Sichan.

sentences.zh: 詔贈高祖兄道談散騎常侍 「道談」北監本、汲本、殿本作「道譚」，原本下卷亦作「道譚」。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted the Founder's elder brother Daotan Gentleman Attendant at the Palace: "Daotan" in the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions read "Daotan" (with speech); the original text of the lower scroll also reads "Daotan."
translations.idiomatic: On "posthumously granted the Founder's brother Daotan Gentleman Attendant": Northern Supervisory, Jigu, Hall, and juan 2 read Daotan with the speech radical.

sentences.zh: 今以譚談字同，不改歸一律。

translations.literal: Now because Tan and Tan are the same character, they are not normalized to one form.
translations.idiomatic: Tan and Tan are treated as the same character and not forced to one spelling.

sentences.zh: 食邑各二千戶 按南康愍王曇朗傳，休先追封為武康縣公時，邑一千戶，其後追封南康郡王，始食二千戶。

translations.literal: Fief households each two thousand: comment—according to the biography of Prince Min of Nankang Tanlang, when Xiuxian was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Wukang county, the fief was one thousand households; afterward when posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Nankang commandery, he then received two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: On "fief two thousand households each": Prince Min of Nankang's biography gives Xiuxian one thousand households as Duke of Wukang and two thousand only as Prince of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 此「二千戶」當作「一千戶」。

translations.literal: This "two thousand households" should read "one thousand households."
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand households here should be one thousand.

sentences.zh: 遣其將歐陽頠傅泰及其子孜為前軍 按《梁書·敬帝紀》，孜乃蕭勃從子，此云「及其子孜」，疑脫一「從」字。

translations.literal: Sent his generals Ouyang Wei, Fu Tai, and his son Zi as the vanguard army: comment—according to the Annals of the Deposed Emperor in the Book of Liang, Zi was Xiao Bo's younger brother's son; here it says "and his son Zi"—suspected omission of one character "younger brother's."
translations.idiomatic: On "sent Ouyang Wei, Fu Tai, and his son Zi as vanguard": the Book of Liang makes Zi Bo's nephew; "his son" may lack younger brother's.

sentences.zh: 大極交越 「極」北監本、汲本、殿本作「拯」。

translations.literal: Great Ultimate reaching Jiao and Yue: "Ultimate" in the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions read "Rescue."
translations.idiomatic: On "Great Ultimate reaching Jiao and Yue": Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall read Rescue for Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 按極訓至，「大極」與上「遠踰」相對成文，作「極」是。

translations.literal: Comment: ultimate is glossed as "reach"; "Great Ultimate" pairs with "far surpassing" above to form the text—writing "Ultimate" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Ultimate means reach; Great Ultimate pairs with far surpassing above—Ultimate is correct.

sentences.zh: 「典澈」或本作「曲澈」，前有「典澈湖」亦同，皆疑。

translations.literal: "Dian Che" may originally have read "Qu Che"; the earlier "Dian Che Lake" is the same—all doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Dian Che may have been Qu Che, as with Dian Che Lake above—all uncertain.

sentences.zh: 公龍驤虎步 按唐人避諱，「虎」皆改為「武」，此「虎」字乃後人回改。

translations.literal: The Duke's dragon soar and tiger stride: comment—under Tang taboo avoidance, "tiger" is everywhere changed to "martial"; this "tiger" character is a later restoration.
translations.idiomatic: On "dragon soar and tiger stride": Tang taboo changed tiger to martial; this tiger is a later restoration.

sentences.zh: 裁舉靈

translations.literal: Cut and raised the spirit
translations.idiomatic: Cut and raised the spirit

translations.idiomatic: (chu)

sentences.zh: [⓪]據北監本、汲本、殿本及南史、元龜一八六改。

translations.literal: [⓪]—corrected according to the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, Hall editions and the Southern History and Yuan Gui 186.
translations.idiomatic: [⓪]—emended per Northern Supervisory, Jigu, Hall, Southern History, and Yuan Gui 186.

sentences.zh: 按「靈刍」南監本作「靈旗」。

translations.literal: Comment: "spirit chu" in the Southern Supervisory edition reads "spirit banner."
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Supervisory edition reads spirit banner for spirit chu.

sentences.zh: 噎

translations.literal: Choked
translations.idiomatic: Choked

translations.idiomatic: (zhi)

sentences.zh: [濉]水而不流 據南監本改。

translations.literal: [Sui] River and it did not flow: corrected according to the Southern Supervisory edition.
translations.idiomatic: [Sui] River and it did not flow: emended per the Southern Supervisory edition.

sentences.zh: 按元龜一八六作「睢水」，今行徐孝穆文集多作「濉水」。

translations.literal: Comment: Yuan Gui 186 reads "Sui River"; the current Xiao Tong literary collection mostly reads "Si River."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Gui 186 reads Sui River; most received texts of Xu Ling's anthology read Si River.

sentences.zh: 史記高祖本紀有「睢水為之不流」語，以作「睢水」或「濉水」為是。

translations.literal: The Basic Annals of Gaozu in the Records of the Grand Historian has the phrase "the Sui River ceased to flow for it"—to write either "Sui River" or "Si River" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji's Gaozu annals says the Sui River ceased to flow—either Sui or Si River is defensible.

sentences.zh: 卓爾英狀 「英狀」元龜一八六作「英猷」，疑作「英猷」是。

translations.literal: Outstanding heroic form: "heroic form" Yuan Gui 186 reads "heroic design"—suspected that "heroic design" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: On "outstanding heroic form": Yuan Gui 186 reads heroic design, which may be correct.

sentences.zh: 多歷歲時 「多」原本訛「各」，南監本訛「名」，今據北監本、汲本、殿本改正。

translations.literal: Many years passed: "many" was originally corrupted to "each"; the Southern Supervisory edition misread "name"; now corrected according to the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "through many years": the text originally read each for many and the Southern Supervisory read name; corrected per the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions.

sentences.zh: 吳濞已

translations.literal: Wu Bi already
translations.idiomatic: Wu Bi already

translations.literal: (cong)
translations.idiomatic: (cong)

sentences.zh: [鏦]據《南史·陳武帝紀》改。

translations.literal: [Cong]—corrected according to the Annals of Emperor Wu in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: [Cong]—corrected per the Southern Dynasties Annals of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 按史記吳王濞傳「使人鏦殺吳王」，為此語所本。

translations.literal: Comment: the Biography of King Bi of Wu in the Records of the Grand Historian reads "had someone cong-kill the King of Wu"—this phrase derives from it.
translations.idiomatic: The Records' Biography of King Bi of Wu reads "had someone cong-kill the King of Wu"—this line comes from there.

sentences.zh: 鏦，撞也，摐亦訓撞，然當從史記作「鏦」。

translations.literal: Comment: cong means strike; cheng also means strike, but the text should follow the Records and read cong.
translations.idiomatic: Note: cong means to strike and cheng likewise, but the Records' reading cong should be followed.

sentences.zh: 金獸符第一至第五左 「金獸符」即「金虎符」，此避唐諱改。

translations.literal: Gold beast tally, first through fifth, left: "gold beast tally" is "gold tiger tally"—changed to avoid Tang taboo.
translations.idiomatic: On "gold beast tally, first through fifth, left": gold beast tally is gold tiger tally, emended for Tang taboo.

sentences.zh: 竹使符第一至第十[左]據《南史·陳武帝紀》補。

translations.literal: Bamboo envoy tally, first through tenth [left]—[left] supplied according to the Annals of Emperor Wu in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: On "bamboo envoy tally, first through tenth [left]": left restored per the Southern Dynasties Annals of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 按符制，虎符、竹使符均剖分為左右。

translations.literal: Comment: under the tally system, tiger tallies and bamboo envoy tallies were each split into left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Under the tally system, tiger tallies and bamboo envoy tallies were each divided into left and right halves.

sentences.zh: 是用錫公武賁之士三百人 按「武賁」即「虎賁」，此避唐諱改。

translations.literal: Therefore grant to the Duke three hundred warriors of the martial guard: "martial guard" is "tiger guard"—changed to avoid Tang taboo.
translations.idiomatic: On "grant the Duke three hundred warriors of the martial guard": martial guard is tiger guard, changed for Tang taboo.

sentences.zh: 微微皇極 汲本「微微」下有小注，云一作「徽徽」。

translations.literal: Faintly the imperial apex: the Jigu edition has a small note below "faintly faintly" reading "also written huihui."
translations.idiomatic: On "faintly the imperial apex": the Jigu edition notes below faintly faintly an alternate reading huihui.

sentences.zh: 北監本、殿本及《南史·陳武帝紀》並作「徽徽」。

translations.literal: The Northern Supervisory, Hall editions, and the Annals of Emperor Wu in the History of the Southern Dynasties all read huihui.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Supervisory, Hall editions, and the Southern Dynasties Annals of Emperor Wu all read huihui.

sentences.zh: 按張元濟

translations.literal: Comment: Zhang Yuanji
translations.idiomatic: Comment: Zhang Yuanji

sentences.zh: 〈校勘記〉

translations.literal: 〈Collation note〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Collation note〉

sentences.zh: 云作「微微」是。

translations.literal: says: "Reading faintly faintly is correct."
translations.idiomatic: argues that reading faintly faintly is correct.

sentences.zh: 龍行武步 「武步」即「虎步」，此避唐諱改。

translations.literal: Dragon gait, martial stride: "martial stride" is "tiger stride"—changed to avoid Tang taboo.
translations.idiomatic: On "dragon gait, martial stride": martial stride is tiger stride, changed for Tang taboo.

sentences.zh: 凶渠傳首 「渠」原訛「集」，各本不訛，今改正。

translations.literal: The vicious chieftain's head sent: "chieftain" was originally corrupted to "gather"; other editions are not corrupt; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: On "the vicious chieftain's head sent": qu was originally miswritten as ji; other editions are correct; emended.

sentences.zh: 下漏深泉 「深泉」即「淵泉」，此避唐諱改。

translations.literal: The clepsydra drips into the deep spring: "deep spring" is "abyss spring"—changed to avoid Tang taboo.
translations.idiomatic: On "the clepsydra drips into the deep spring": deep spring is abyss spring, changed for Tang taboo.

sentences.zh: 時乘御

translations.literal: When riding the times, governing
translations.idiomatic: When riding the times, governing

translations.literal: (bian)
translations.idiomatic: (bian)

sentences.zh: [宇]據南監本改。

translations.literal: [Yu]—corrected according to the Southern Supervisory edition.
translations.idiomatic: [Yu]—corrected per the Southern Supervisory edition.

sentences.zh: 按殿本亦從南監本改。

translations.literal: Comment: the Hall edition also follows the Southern Supervisory in the change.
translations.idiomatic: The Hall edition likewise follows the Southern Supervisory emendation.

sentences.zh: 今遣使持節兼太保侍中尚書左僕射平樂亭侯王通 按

translations.literal: Now dispatching the envoy bearing staff of office, concurrent Grand Tutor, Palace Attendant, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Marquis of Pingle precinct, Wang Tong—comment:
translations.idiomatic: On "Now dispatching the envoy bearing staff, concurrent Grand Tutor, Palace Attendant, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Marquis of Pingle precinct, Wang Tong"—note:

sentences.zh: 〈王通傳〉

translations.literal: 〈Biography of Wang Tong〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Biography of Wang Tong〉

sentences.zh: ，通仕梁為尚書右僕射，入陳始遷左僕射。

translations.literal: reads: "Tong served Liang as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and only on entering Chen was transferred to Left Vice Director."
translations.idiomatic: reads: Tong served Liang as right vice director of the Masters of Writing and was not moved to left vice director until he entered Chen.

sentences.zh: 又通以帝甥封武陽亭侯。

translations.literal: Moreover Tong, as the emperor's sister's son, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuyang precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as the emperor's sister's son, he was enfeoffed Marquis of Wuyang precinct.

sentences.zh: 紀傳互異。

translations.literal: The annals and biography disagree.
translations.idiomatic: The annals and the biography disagree.
